1.title: From Adam to Abraham
1.context: Genealogies from Adam — Chronicles places redemption history in the cosmic context of creation.

2.title: The Sons of Israel
2.context: Israel's sons — Judah gets the fullest treatment because Messiah will come from this line.

5.title: Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh
5.context: The eastern tribes — even those geographically separated belong to God's people.

6.title: The Levites
6.context: The Levites' line — the priestly family that will lead post-exile worship.

9.title: Returnees in Jerusalem
9.context: Returnees in Jerusalem — Chronicles pivots from pre-exile to post-exile life.

10.title: Saul's Death
10.context: Saul dies — Chronicles barely mentions his reign. The story is really about David.

11.title: David Anointed King
11.context: David anointed king — Chronicles skips ahead to David's triumph. God's promises always come true.

11.title: David's Mighty Warriors
11.context: David's mighty warriors — heroic names recorded. God sees every faithful servant.

13.title: Bringing Back the Ark
13.context: Bringing the ark, the first attempt — zeal without obedience. Uzzah's tragic death.

15.title: The Ark Reaches Jerusalem
15.context: The ark reaches Jerusalem — this time God's way, carried by Levites.

16.title: David's Psalm of Thanks
16.context: David's psalm of thanks — drawn from Psalms 105, 96, 106. A liturgy for the ark's arrival.

17.title: God's Covenant with David
17.context: God's covenant with David — David wants to build God a house; God promises David a dynasty.

21.title: David's Sinful Census
21.context: David's sinful census — Araunah's threshing floor will become the temple site.

22.title: Preparations for the Temple
22.context: Preparations for the temple — David can't build, but provides everything for his son. Father's love.

23.title: Levitical Divisions
23.context: Levitical divisions — worship is not improvised; God's people serve in order.

28.title: David's Charge to Solomon
28.context: David's charge to Solomon — 'Be strong and courageous'. A father's spiritual legacy.

29.title: David's Final Prayer
29.context: David's prayer of dedication — 'All things come from you, and of your own we give'. One of Scripture's most beautiful prayers of stewardship.

1.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
1.context: Solomon asks for wisdom — a humble heart that asks the right thing receives more than was asked.

2.title: Preparations for the Temple
2.context: Temple preparations — international cooperation through Tyrian craftsmen and cedar.

3.title: Solomon Builds the Temple
3.context: Mount Moriah — where Abraham offered Isaac. Now the temple foundation.

5.title: The Ark Enters the Temple
5.context: The ark enters — the high point of Israelite worship history. God's glory fills the temple.

6.title: Solomon's Dedication Prayer
6.context: Solomon's dedication prayer — interceding for Israel, foreigners, and even future exiles.

7.title: The Glory Fills the Temple
7.context: Fire falls from heaven, glory fills the temple — God's most tangible covenant affirmation in history.

9.title: The Queen of Sheba
9.context: The Queen of Sheba — Jesus uses her as an example of Gentiles seeking truth.

10.title: The Kingdom Divides
10.context: The kingdom divides — Rehoboam's harshness splits Israel forever.

14.title: Asa's Reforms
14.context: Asa's reforms — an early revival in the south. 'O LORD, help us!'

17.title: Jehoshaphat's Reforms
17.context: Jehoshaphat's reforms — instituting law, teaching, and a faithful military.

20.title: Jehoshaphat's Prayer and Victory
20.context: Jehoshaphat's prayer — 'We don't know what to do, but our eyes are on you'. Then he sends singers ahead of the army.

24.title: Joash Repairs the Temple
24.context: Joash repairs the temple — a young king responds to a priest's guidance and rebuilds worship.

29.title: Hezekiah Purifies the Temple
29.context: Hezekiah cleans the temple — every revival begins with the temple, not the throne.

30.title: Hezekiah's Passover
30.context: Hezekiah's Passover — relighting the flame of national worship.

32.title: Sennacherib's Invasion
32.context: Sennacherib's invasion — Hezekiah trusts, and God strikes down 185,000 Assyrians.

33.title: Manasseh Repents
33.context: Manasseh's repentance — only Chronicles records the worst king's late conversion. God's grace is sufficient for anyone.

34.title: Josiah's Reforms
34.context: Josiah — at age 8 he begins to seek God. 'While he was still young.'

34.title: The Book of the Law Found
34.context: The Book of the Law found — long forgotten. Josiah tears his clothes upon hearing it read.

36.title: Judah's Last Kings
36.context: Judah's last kings — each worse than the last. The end is near.

36.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
36.context: 'Beyond remedy' — the limit of God's long patience. Exile becomes inevitable.

36.title: The Decree of Cyrus
36.context: Old Testament ends — Cyrus's decree. A final ray of hope in the darkness.

1.title: Cyrus' Decree
1.context: Cyrus's decree — fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy 150 years earlier. A pagan king as God's instrument.

2.title: List of Returnees
2.context: List of returnees — 49,697. A small number, but God's faithful remnant.

3.title: The Altar Rebuilt
3.context: The altar rebuilt first — even before walls or houses. Worship before safety.

3.title: Foundation of the Temple
3.context: The temple foundation laid — old men weep remembering Solomon's temple; young men rejoice. Both are right.

4.title: Opposition Halts the Work
4.context: Opposition halts the work for 16 years. Spiritual work always faces resistance.

5.title: Resumption of Building
5.context: Work resumes — Haggai and Zechariah's prophecies rekindle the fire.

6.title: The Temple Completed
6.context: The temple completed — 20 years later. God's work moves slowly but always finishes.

7.title: Ezra Comes to Jerusalem
7.context: Ezra arrives — 80 years after the first wave. His focus: worship and teaching.

9.title: Ezra's Prayer of Confession
9.context: Ezra mourns the people's sin — true leadership intercedes for sin instead of excusing it.

10.title: The People Confess
10.context: The people confess — Ezra's tears spark national repentance.

1.title: Nehemiah's Prayer
1.context: Nehemiah's prayer — a royal cupbearer weeps for Jerusalem. God raises unlikely leaders.

2.title: Artaxerxes Sends Nehemiah
2.context: Nehemiah's request — after four months of prayer, he speaks. 'I prayed to the God of heaven' — even mid-conversation with the king.

2.title: Inspecting the Walls
2.context: Inspecting the walls at night — a leader gathers facts before making plans.

3.title: Builders of the Walls
3.context: Builders of the walls — every name listed. God remembers each faithful worker.

4.title: Opposition to the Work
4.context: Opposition mocks the work — 'I cannot come down; the work is too important'. The mark of spiritual work.

5.title: Nehemiah Helps the Poor
5.context: Helping the poor — a real leader cares about the practical struggles of his people.

6.title: The Wall Completed
6.context: Wall finished in 52 days — 'This work has been done by our God'. Achievements that defy human explanation.

8.title: Ezra Reads the Law
8.context: Ezra reads the Law — a multi-day Bible conference. God's word brings repentance.

9.title: Israelites Confess Their Sins
9.context: Confession and covenant — reviewing Israel's history, owning their failures and God's faithfulness.

12.title: Dedication of the Wall
12.context: Dedication of the wall — joy and music fill the city, heard from afar.

13.title: Nehemiah's Final Reforms
13.context: Nehemiah's final reforms — old problems creep back. Spiritual work never stops.

1.title: Queen Vashti Deposed
1.context: Xerxes' feast — an opening scene of breathtaking excess and folly.

2.title: Esther Made Queen
2.context: Esther becomes queen — a Jewish orphan rises to Persia's throne. God's hidden hand.

2.title: Mordecai Uncovers a Plot
2.context: Mordecai uncovers a plot — a forgotten kindness that will save lives years later. God remembers.

3.title: Haman's Plot
3.context: Haman's plot — the root of antisemitism that has been replayed countless times in history.

4.title: Mordecai Persuades Esther
4.context: Mordecai persuades Esther — 'You will not escape'. Even in the palace, no Jewish woman is safe.

4.title: For Such a Time as This
4.context: 'For such a time as this' — Mordecai's challenge propels Esther toward her riskiest act. God's providence meets human courage.

5.title: Esther's Request
5.context: Esther's request — long-prepared, finally the moment of decision.

6.title: Mordecai Honored
6.context: Mordecai honored — the king's sleepless night turns the whole plot.

7.title: Haman Hanged
7.context: Haman hanged — on the very gallows he built. Psalm 9:15 fulfilled.

8.title: The King's Edict for the Jews
8.context: The king's edict for the Jews — Esther and Mordecai turn destruction into deliverance.

9.title: The Triumph of the Jews
9.context: The Jewish triumph — the day meant for destruction becomes a day of celebration.

9.title: Purim Established
9.context: Purim established — still one of Judaism's most joyful festivals. God's providence never sleeps.

1.title: Job's Character and Trial
1.context: Job's character — 'blameless and upright'. Among the highest praise Scripture gives anyone.

1.title: Job's First Test
1.context: Job's first test — wealth and children lost in one day. He still worships: 'The LORD gave; the LORD has taken away.'

2.title: Job's Second Test
2.context: Second test — his body afflicted. His wife: 'Curse God and die.' Job does not sin with his lips.

2.title: Job's Three Friends
2.context: Three friends come — and sit in silence seven days. This is their best moment.

3.title: Job's Lament
3.context: Job's lament — cursing his birthday. Honest grief, not sinful rebellion.

4.title: Eliphaz Speaks
4.context: Eliphaz speaks — 'The innocent never suffer'. Sounds pious, but is wrong.

8.title: Bildad Speaks
8.context: Bildad speaks — quoting ancient wisdom. True statements, wrong application.

11.title: Zophar Speaks
11.context: Zophar speaks — the harshest of the three. 'God is treating you better than you deserve'. Deeply wrong.

15.title: Eliphaz Speaks Again
15.context: Eliphaz speaks again — the friends sharpen their accusations. Job holds his innocence.

19.title: My Redeemer Lives
19.context: 'I know my Redeemer lives' — from his ash heap, Job sees through to resurrection. A stunning preview of Christ's work.

28.title: A Hymn to Wisdom
28.context: A hymn to wisdom — 'But where can wisdom be found?' The book's central reflection.

32.title: Elihu Speaks
32.context: Elihu speaks — young, passionate, self-confident. Yet his words prepare Job to hear God.

38.title: The LORD Speaks from the Whirlwind
38.context: The LORD answers from the whirlwind — after 37 chapters of debate, God appears. He doesn't explain why, but reveals himself.

40.title: Job's Response
40.context: Job's response — 'I lay my hand on my mouth'. Seeing God's greatness silences every argument.

40.title: God Speaks Again
40.context: God speaks again — describing Behemoth and Leviathan. God's universe is far vaster than human sight.

42.title: Job's Repentance and Restoration
42.context: Job repents and is restored — 'I repent'. God not only answers but doubles his blessings.

1.title: The Way of the Righteous
1.context: The doorway to the Psalms. Two paths, two destinies — and the wise are those who delight in God's instruction day and night.

2.title: The Reign of the Lord's Anointed
2.context: A messianic coronation psalm quoted repeatedly in the New Testament. The kings of earth rage in vain against the Anointed One God himself has installed.

3.title: Morning Prayer of Trust
3.context: Written when David fled Absalom. God as shield in the deepest crisis.

4.title: Evening Prayer of Trust
4.context: An evening prayer — sleeping in trust even with enemies all around.

5.title: Morning Prayer for Guidance
5.context: Morning prayer — 'Listen to my words, LORD'.

6.title: Prayer in Time of Distress
6.context: The first of seven penitential psalms. Crying for healing in illness.

7.title: A Plea for Justice
7.context: When falsely accused — pleading with God for vindication.

8.title: God's Glory and Human Dignity
8.context: A meditation under the stars: 'What is man that you are mindful of him?' Quoted in Hebrews 2 to describe Christ — the true Son of Man.

9.title: Praise for God's Righteous Judgments
9.context: Praise for righteous judgments — a victory song.

10.title: A Cry Against Wickedness
10.context: 'Why, LORD, do you stand far off?' Honest cry from one who feels abandoned.

11.title: Refuge in the LORD
11.context: 'In the LORD I take refuge' — refusing to yield to fear.

12.title: A Plea Against Liars
12.context: 'The words of the LORD are flawless' — a plea against deceit.

13.title: How Long, O LORD?
13.context: 'How long, O LORD?' One of the most-cited laments. The honest cry of waiting.

14.title: The Folly of Atheism
14.context: The fool says 'There is no God' — wisdom begins with acknowledging him.

15.title: Who Shall Dwell on Your Holy Hill?
15.context: Who shall dwell on your holy hill? — A description of the righteous.

16.title: My Chosen Portion
16.context: 'My chosen portion' — Acts 2 cites this as a prophecy of Christ's resurrection.

17.title: A Prayer of David
17.context: A prayer of David — 'Hide me in the shadow of your wings'.

18.title: David's Song of Deliverance
18.context: David's song of deliverance — a life-spanning thanksgiving. Same as 2 Samuel 22.

19.title: The Heavens Declare God's Glory
19.context: The heavens declare God's glory — creation and Scripture are God's two books. The psalmist moves from one to the other.

20.title: Trust in the Name of the LORD
20.context: Prayer for the king's victory — sung before battle.

21.title: Praise for Victory
21.context: Praise after victory — the bookend to Psalm 20.

22.title: From Suffering to Praise
22.context: The cry Jesus echoed from the cross. Centuries before Calvary, David describes pierced hands and feet, mocking onlookers, and gambling for clothing.

23.title: The LORD Is My Shepherd
23.context: Perhaps the most beloved chapter in all Scripture. Through danger, fear, and even the valley of death's shadow, the believer is shepherded — not abandoned.

24.title: The King of Glory
24.context: 'The earth is the LORD's' — the King of Glory enters his temple.

25.title: Teach Me Your Paths
25.context: An acrostic prayer — for guidance and forgiveness.

26.title: Plea of an Innocent Man
26.context: Plea of an innocent man — honesty before God.

27.title: The LORD My Light
27.context: 'The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?' A psalm of bold trust spoken into the darkness.

28.title: A Cry for Help
28.context: 'My rock, do not turn a deaf ear' — a cry for response.

29.title: The Voice of the LORD
29.context: The voice of the LORD — a thunderstorm as a picture of divine power.

30.title: Thanksgiving for Deliverance
30.context: Thanksgiving for healing — 'His anger is but for a moment, his favor is for a lifetime'.

31.title: Into Your Hand I Commit My Spirit
31.context: 'Into your hands I commit my spirit' — Jesus' final words on the cross.

32.title: The Joy of Forgiveness
32.context: Joy of forgiveness — possibly David's reflection after Bathsheba.

33.title: Praise to the Creator
33.context: Praise to the Creator — 'By the word of the LORD the heavens were made'.

34.title: Taste and See the LORD Is Good
34.context: Taste and see — 'Blessed is the one who takes refuge in him'. Cited in 1 Peter 2:3.

35.title: Prayer for Rescue
35.context: Prayer for rescue — David surrounded by deceitful enemies.

36.title: God's Steadfast Love
36.context: God's steadfast love — 'Your love, O LORD, reaches to the heavens'.

37.title: Do Not Fret Because of Evildoers
37.context: Do not fret because of evildoers — a wisdom psalm.

38.title: Prayer of a Suffering Penitent
38.context: A penitential psalm — pleading for healing in body and soul.

39.title: Life Is Fleeting
39.context: Life is fleeting — 'My days are a few handbreadths'.

40.title: A Song of Deliverance
40.context: 'I waited patiently for the LORD' — Hebrews 10 cites this as Christ's words.

41.title: Blessed Is He Who Considers the Poor
41.context: Blessed is he who considers the poor — Jesus quotes 'one who shares my bread' at the Last Supper.

42.title: As the Deer Pants for Water
42.context: 'As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul pants for you, O God.' A psalm of depression that still preaches to its own soul.

43.title: Send Out Your Light
43.context: Send out your light — a continuation of Psalm 42.

44.title: A Plea for National Restoration
44.context: A plea for national restoration — after a national tragedy.

45.title: The Royal Wedding Song
45.context: The royal wedding song — Hebrews 1 cites it as a messianic psalm.

46.title: God Is Our Refuge
46.context: 'God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.' Martin Luther's 'A Mighty Fortress' draws its language from this psalm.

47.title: God the King of All Earth
47.context: God the King of all earth — clapping and shouting in praise.

48.title: The Glory of Zion
48.context: The glory of Zion — praising God's city.

49.title: The Folly of Trusting in Riches
49.context: The folly of trusting in riches — 'You cannot take it with you'.

50.title: True Worship
50.context: True worship — God needs no animals; he needs the heart.

51.title: Create in Me a Clean Heart
51.context: David's cry of repentance after his sin with Bathsheba. Every fallen believer who has dared to hope in God's mercy finds words here.

52.title: Judgment on the Deceitful
52.context: Judgment on the deceitful Doeg — written after Saul's massacre at Nob.

53.title: The Folly of Atheism
53.context: The folly of atheism — a slight variation of Psalm 14.

54.title: Prayer for Vindication
54.context: Prayer for vindication — when the Ziphites betrayed David to Saul.

55.title: Betrayed by a Friend
55.context: Betrayed by a friend — 'It is not an enemy who insults me'. Possibly anticipating Judas.

56.title: In God I Trust
56.context: 'When I am afraid, I put my trust in you' — the prayer of the brave.

57.title: Steadfast Heart in Trouble
57.context: Composed in a cave — David hiding from Saul, still able to praise.

58.title: A Plea Against Injustice
58.context: A plea against injustice — one of the rare 'imprecatory psalms'.

59.title: Deliverance from Enemies
59.context: Deliverance from enemies — when Saul sent men to watch David's house.

60.title: Restore Us, O God
60.context: Restore us, O God — after a national defeat.

61.title: Lead Me to the Rock
61.context: Lead me to the rock — possibly during exile or extreme distress.

62.title: My Soul Waits in Silence
62.context: My soul waits in silence — a song of trust.

63.title: My Soul Thirsts for You
63.context: My soul thirsts for you — written in the wilderness of Judah.

64.title: Protection from Hidden Plots
64.context: Protection from hidden plots — safety from secret schemes.

65.title: Thanksgiving for Earth's Bounty
65.context: Thanksgiving for earth's bounty — God's blessing on the harvest.

66.title: All the Earth Worships God
66.context: All the earth worships — bearing witness to God's wonders.

67.title: May All Peoples Praise God
67.context: May all peoples praise — that the nations may know God.

68.title: Sing to God, You Kingdoms
68.context: Sing to God — when the ark went up to Zion. Ephesians 4:8 cites this for Christ's ascension.

69.title: Save Me, O God
69.context: Save me, O God — Acts cites 'May his place be deserted' regarding Judas.

70.title: Urgent Prayer for Help
70.context: Urgent prayer for help — a brief, intense plea.

71.title: Prayer in Old Age
71.context: Prayer in old age — a lifelong trust into the gray years.

72.title: Prayer for the King
72.context: Prayer for the king — by or for Solomon. A foreshadow of Christ's reign.

73.title: The Tempting Prosperity of the Wicked
73.context: Why do the wicked prosper — until Asaph enters the sanctuary and sees their end.

74.title: Lament for the Sanctuary
74.context: Lament for the sanctuary — likely after 586 BCE.

75.title: God Is the Judge
75.context: God is the judge — 'I will lift up the righteous'.

76.title: God Is Victorious
76.context: God is victorious — possibly after the Assyrian defeat in Hezekiah's day.

77.title: Comfort in Dark Night
77.context: Comfort in dark night — Asaph recalls God's deeds and finds peace again.

78.title: Tell the Coming Generation
78.context: Tell the coming generation — Israel's history must be passed on.

79.title: Lament Over Jerusalem
79.context: Lament over Jerusalem — like Psalm 74, likely from after the destruction.

80.title: Restore Us, O God
80.context: Restore us — 'O Shepherd of Israel' — pleading using the vineyard image.

81.title: Song for Festival
81.context: A festival song — possibly for the Feast of Tabernacles.

82.title: God Stands in Judgment
82.context: God stands in judgment — Jesus quotes this in John 10:34.

83.title: Plea Against Israel's Enemies
83.context: Plea against Israel's enemies — an imprecatory psalm.

84.title: How Lovely Is Your Dwelling Place
84.context: How lovely is your dwelling place — 'Better one day in your courts than a thousand elsewhere'. A pilgrim's heart.

85.title: Revive Us Again
85.context: Revive us again — a post-exilic prayer.

86.title: Hear Me, O LORD
86.context: Hear me, O LORD — a personal prayer of David.

87.title: The Glory of Zion
87.context: The glory of Zion — even Gentile nations will be 'born in Zion'.

88.title: Cry from the Depths
88.context: Cry from the depths — the darkest psalm. It ends without resolution.

89.title: God's Covenant with David
89.context: God's covenant with David — ending with the painful question 'Where is your steadfast love?'

90.title: God Is Eternal
90.context: A psalm of Moses — a meditation on life's brevity. 'Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.'

91.title: The Shelter of the Most High
91.context: A psalm of the safest of all places — under the shadow of the Almighty. Satan misquoted these lines tempting Jesus in the wilderness.

92.title: Song for the Sabbath
92.context: Song for the Sabbath — composed for the day of rest.

93.title: The LORD Reigns
93.context: The LORD reigns — one of four consecutive 'kingship' psalms.

94.title: Vengeance Belongs to God
94.context: Vengeance belongs to God — 'O God of vengeance'.

95.title: Come, Let Us Worship
95.context: Come, let us worship — Hebrews 3 cites this as a warning.

96.title: Sing a New Song
96.context: Sing a new song — related to David's psalm in 1 Chronicles 16.

97.title: The LORD Reigns, Let the Earth Rejoice
97.context: The LORD reigns — kingship enthronement psalm.

98.title: Sing a New Song to the LORD
98.context: Sing a new song to the LORD — echoing Isaiah's 'Holy One of Israel'.

99.title: The LORD Our God Is Holy
99.context: The LORD our God is holy — 'Holy is he' repeated three times.

100.title: A Psalm of Thanksgiving
100.context: A bright song of universal worship. For a thousand years, Christian congregations have begun their services with these joyful lines.

101.title: A King's Resolve
101.context: A king's resolve — David's pledge to govern with integrity.

102.title: Prayer of an Afflicted Man
102.context: Prayer of an afflicted man — Hebrews 1 cites this as the Father speaking to Christ.

103.title: Bless the LORD, O My Soul
103.context: Bless the LORD, O my soul — 'Forget not all his benefits'.

104.title: Praise to the Creator
104.context: Praise to the Creator — a poem of nature, following Genesis 1's order.

105.title: Remember His Wondrous Works
105.context: Remember his wondrous works — Israel's history as a song.

106.title: The LORD's Steadfast Love and Israel's Rebellion
106.context: God's mercy and Israel's rebellion — paired with Psalm 105.

107.title: Give Thanks to the LORD
107.context: Give thanks to the LORD — four groups testify to God's deliverance.

108.title: Through God We Shall Do Valiantly
108.context: Through God we shall do valiantly — combining parts of Psalms 57 and 60.

109.title: Help Me, O LORD My God
109.context: Help me, O God — Acts 1 cites 'May another take his office' regarding Judas.

110.title: The Lord Says to My Lord
110.context: The Lord says to my Lord — the most-quoted Old Testament psalm in the New Testament.

111.title: Great Are the LORD's Works
111.context: Great are the LORD's works — an acrostic wisdom psalm.

112.title: The Blessings of the Righteous
112.context: The blessings of the righteous — 'Blessed is the man who fears the LORD'.

113.title: Praise the Name of the LORD
113.context: Praise the LORD — opening the 'Egyptian Hallel' sung at Passover.

114.title: When Israel Came Out of Egypt
114.context: When Israel came out of Egypt — history transformed into poetry.

115.title: Glory to God Alone
115.context: Glory to God alone — 'Not to us, O LORD, but to your name be glory'.

116.title: Thanksgiving for Deliverance
116.context: Thanksgiving for deliverance — possibly after recovery from illness.

117.title: Praise the LORD, All Nations
117.context: The shortest chapter in the Bible — just two verses calling all nations to praise.

118.title: His Steadfast Love Endures Forever
118.context: His steadfast love endures forever — likely sung by Jesus at the Last Supper.

119.title: The Word of God: A Meditation
119.context: The longest chapter in the Bible — 176 verses in 22 alphabetic sections — a sustained meditation on the beauty and life-giving power of God's word.

120.title: Song of Ascents: Deliver Me
120.context: Songs of Ascents — the first of 15 psalms sung by pilgrims going to Jerusalem.

121.title: My Help Comes from the LORD
121.context: 'I lift up my eyes to the hills — where does my help come from? My help comes from the LORD.' The most beloved of the pilgrim psalms.

122.title: Pray for the Peace of Jerusalem
122.context: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem — 'May they prosper who love you'.

123.title: Our Eyes Look to the LORD
123.context: Our eyes look to the LORD — like a servant's eyes on the master's hand.

124.title: If the LORD Had Not Been on Our Side
124.context: If the LORD had not been on our side — recalling miraculous deliverances.

125.title: Those Who Trust in the LORD
125.context: Those who trust in the LORD — 'They are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken'.

126.title: Restoration of Zion
126.context: Restoration of Zion — likely composed after the return from exile.

127.title: Unless the LORD Builds
127.context: Unless the LORD builds — the only Song of Ascents written by Solomon.

128.title: Blessed Is Everyone Who Fears the LORD
128.context: Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD — family blessings.

129.title: Affliction Cannot Destroy Israel
129.context: Affliction cannot destroy Israel — persecuted from youth, but never crushed.

130.title: Out of the Depths
130.context: 'Out of the depths I cry to you, O LORD.' The penitential psalm Luther called 'a Pauline psalm' — every line drips with grace.

131.title: A Calm and Quiet Soul
131.context: A calm and quiet soul — like a weaned child with its mother.

132.title: Remember David and His Vow
132.context: Remember David — Zion will be God's eternal dwelling.

133.title: When Brothers Dwell in Unity
133.context: When brothers dwell in unity — 'How good and pleasant!'

134.title: Bless the LORD by Night
134.context: Bless the LORD by night — a benediction for the temple priests.

135.title: Praise the LORD
135.context: Praise the LORD — drawing from many other psalms.

136.title: His Steadfast Love Endures Forever
136.context: His steadfast love endures forever — 26 repetitions of the refrain.

137.title: By the Waters of Babylon
137.context: By the waters of Babylon — exile's grief.

138.title: Thanksgiving for Answered Prayer
138.context: Thanksgiving for answered prayer — 'The lofty he sees from afar'.

139.title: God Knows Me Completely
139.context: The Bible's deepest meditation on divine omniscience. There is no height, depth, or darkness where God's hand cannot reach the believer.

140.title: Deliver Me from Evil Men
140.context: Deliver me from evil men — David's plea for protection.

141.title: Evening Prayer for Protection
141.context: Evening prayer — 'May my prayer be like incense before you'.

142.title: Cry from the Cave
142.context: Cry from the cave — written when David hid from Saul.

143.title: Lead Me in the Way I Should Go
143.context: The seventh penitential psalm — 'Teach me your way'.

144.title: My Rock and My Fortress
144.context: My rock and my fortress — pleading for deliverance through many images.

145.title: Great Is the LORD
145.context: Great is the LORD — the last psalm specifically attributed to David.

146.title: Praise the LORD, O My Soul
146.context: Praise the LORD, O my soul — opening the final five 'Hallelujah' psalms.

147.title: Praise the LORD Who Heals
147.context: Praise the LORD who heals — 'He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds'.

148.title: Let All Creation Praise
148.context: Let all creation praise — heavens, depths, kings, animals — all called to worship.

149.title: Sing a New Song
149.context: Sing a new song — even the second-to-last psalm calls for newness.

150.title: Praise the LORD with All Instruments
150.context: The final psalm — pure, distilled praise. From the deepest lament (Psalm 22) to the highest acclamation (Psalm 150), all of life ends in worship.

1.title: The Beginning of Knowledge
1.context: The beginning of knowledge — the fear of the LORD as the bedrock of all wisdom.

1.title: The Call of Wisdom
1.context: Wisdom calls aloud in the streets — not hidden, freely available to whoever listens.

2.title: The Value of Wisdom
2.context: The value of wisdom — more precious than gold. Seek, ask, treasure.

3.title: Trust in the LORD
3.context: 'Trust in the LORD with all your heart' — one of the most beloved verses in Proverbs.

4.title: A Father's Wisdom
4.context: A father's wisdom — 'Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it'.

5.title: Warning Against Adultery
5.context: Warning against adultery — the temptation that has destroyed countless young men.

6.title: Things the LORD Hates
6.context: Six things the LORD hates — including 'one who stirs up conflict'. Things to flee from.

7.title: Beware the Adulteress
7.context: Beware the adulteress — a dramatic story showing how seduction works step by step.

8.title: Wisdom's Call
8.context: Wisdom personified — 'I was set up from everlasting'. The New Testament calls Christ 'the wisdom of God'.

9.title: Wisdom and Folly
9.context: Two contrasting hostesses — Wisdom's banquet vs. Folly's seduction. The book's two paths.

10.title: Proverbs of Solomon I
10.context: Solomon's proverbs — short, standalone sayings touching every area of life.

22.title: Sayings of the Wise
22.context: Sayings of the wise — a separate collection, ending in 'thirty sayings of the wise'.

25.title: More Proverbs of Solomon
25.context: More Solomonic proverbs — preserved by Hezekiah's scribes 250 years later.

30.title: The Words of Agur
30.context: The words of Agur — including the prayer 'Give me neither poverty nor riches'.

31.title: The Words of King Lemuel
31.context: King Lemuel's mother — wisdom from a queen mother to a royal son.

31.title: The Wife of Noble Character
31.context: The 'wife of noble character' — written as a Hebrew acrostic. The summation of Proverbs' picture of skillful, godly living.

1.title: Vanity of Vanities
1.context: 'Vanity of vanities' — repeated 38 times in this short book. Life apart from God is meaningless.

1.title: Wisdom Is Vanity
1.context: Wisdom too is vanity — the Preacher tests it firsthand. Wisdom is not the ultimate answer.

2.title: Pleasure Is Vanity
2.context: Pleasure is vanity — the Preacher tries everything: wealth, pleasure, art, learning. None satisfies.

3.title: A Time for Everything
3.context: 'For everything there is a season.' A meditation on life's rhythms — a reminder that God reigns over every season we live through.

5.title: Fear God
5.context: Fear God — the book's central counsel. God is God, and we are not.

7.title: Wisdom in Contrast
7.context: Wisdom in contrast — a series of paradoxes: 'Sorrow is better than laughter'.

9.title: One Fate for All
9.context: One fate for all — death levels everyone.

11.title: Cast Your Bread
11.context: 'Cast your bread upon the waters' — bold generosity even in uncertainty.

12.title: Remember Your Creator
12.context: The book's peak: 'Remember your Creator in the days of your youth.' Then a stunning poetic portrait of aging and death.

12.title: The Conclusion
12.context: The conclusion — 'Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man'.

1.title: The Bride's Longing
1.context: The bride's longing — a direct, honest, intense love poem.

2.title: Love in the Field
2.context: Love in the field — 'I am a rose of Sharon'. Love blooming like spring.

3.title: Night Search
3.context: Night search — lost and found in a dream. Love includes longing and unease.

4.title: Praise of the Bride
4.context: The bridegroom's praise — 'How delightful is your love'. Honor in romance.

5.title: The Bride's Search
5.context: Separation and reunion — distance makes union sweeter.

6.title: Praise Renewed
6.context: Praise renewed — true love never grows tired of describing the beloved.

7.title: Beauty of the Bride
7.context: Beauty of the bride — one of literature's richest celebrations of bodily beauty.

8.title: Love Strong as Death
8.context: Love strong as death — the song's climactic declaration. Love cannot be quenched by any force.

1.title: A Rebellious Nation
1.context: The LORD's indictment — 'Israel does not know; my people do not understand.' The book opens with judgment.

2.title: The Mountain of the LORD
2.context: The mountain of the LORD — Isaiah's grand vision of all nations streaming to God.

5.title: The Song of the Vineyard
5.context: The vineyard song — God's vineyard doesn't yield grapes. Jesus uses this image in his parables.

6.title: Isaiah's Call
6.context: Isaiah's call vision — God on the throne, seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy.' One encounter that reshapes the rest of his life.

7.title: The Sign of Immanuel
7.context: The Immanuel sign — 'God with us'. Matthew 1 cites this fulfilled in Christ's birth.

9.title: A Child Is Born to Us
9.context: 'For unto us a child is born…' The classic Christmas text — and one of the Old Testament's most explicit messianic titles for Jesus.

11.title: The Reign of Jesse's Branch
11.context: The messianic 'Branch from Jesse's root' — a recurring image in Isaiah, fulfilled in Jesus, son of David, son of Jesse.

13.title: Prophecy Against Babylon
13.context: Prophecy against Babylon — Isaiah foretells this superpower's fall, fulfilled 160 years later.

14.title: The Fall of Lucifer
14.context: Lucifer's fall — often read as Satan, but primarily a prophecy against the king of Babylon.

24.title: Judgment on the Earth
24.context: Judgment on the earth — apocalyptic vision begins. God will judge not just one nation but all.

25.title: Praise to the LORD
25.context: Praise on Zion — 'He will swallow up death forever'. Revelation 21 picks up this image.

26.title: A Song of Trust
26.context: A song of trust — 'You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are stayed on you'.

35.title: The Joy of the Redeemed
35.context: The joy of the redeemed — a beautiful poem of hope. John the Baptist quotes it preparing the way.

36.title: Sennacherib's Threat
36.context: Sennacherib's threat — the central historical episode in Isaiah. Promises tested in political crisis.

38.title: Hezekiah's Illness
38.context: Hezekiah's illness healed — his prayer wins fifteen years. In those years he fathers wicked Manasseh.

40.title: Comfort My People
40.context: Isaiah pivots from judgment to comfort: 'Comfort my people.' The New Testament uses these very words to introduce John the Baptist.

40.title: Who Can Compare with God?
40.context: 'Who can compare with God?' — one of the highest theological peaks in all human literature.

42.title: The LORD's Servant
42.context: The Servant of the LORD — first 'Servant Song'. Matthew 12 applies it to Jesus.

43.title: Israel Redeemed
43.context: 'I have redeemed you' — God's tender promise: 'When you pass through the waters, I will be with you'.

45.title: Cyrus Named
45.context: Cyrus named — 150 years before he was born. Isaiah names the future Persian king.

49.title: A Light to the Nations
49.context: A light to the nations — the Servant's mission goes beyond Israel to all peoples.

52.title: The Suffering Servant Begins
52.context: The Suffering Servant song begins — the prophecy that has shaped Christian faith for 2000 years.

53.title: He Was Pierced for Our Transgressions
53.context: Written 700 years before Calvary — the most detailed prophecy of substitutionary atonement in the Old Testament. Every line maps onto Christ's cross.

55.title: Come, Buy Without Money
55.context: Come, buy without money — 'All who thirst, come to the waters'. Jesus echoes this invitation in John 7.

58.title: True Fasting
58.context: True fasting — not outward show, but 'to loose the chains of injustice'. The foundation of biblical justice.

60.title: The Glory of Zion
60.context: 'Arise, shine, for your light has come!' — Revelation 21 echoes these words for the New Jerusalem.

61.title: Good News for the Afflicted
61.context: 'The Spirit of the LORD is on me to preach good news' — Jesus reads this in Nazareth and announces his mission.

65.title: New Heavens and New Earth
65.context: 'Behold, I create new heavens and a new earth.' Isaiah voices the Bible's greatest hope — fulfilled in Revelation 21.

1.title: The Call of Jeremiah
1.context: Jeremiah called before he was even born: 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.' A powerful reminder that God's calling precedes our awareness.

2.title: Israel Forsakes God
2.context: Israel forsakes God — 'They have forsaken me, the spring of living water, and dug their own broken cisterns'.

3.title: A Call to Repent
3.context: A call to repent — even in judgment, God's invitation: come back.

7.title: The Temple Sermon
7.context: The temple sermon — exposing false faith: 'The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD'. Jesus later echoes this.

10.title: Idols vs. the True God
10.context: False gods vs. the true God — Jeremiah's biting satire of wooden idols.

15.title: Jeremiah's Lament
15.context: Jeremiah's lament — 'Woe to me, my mother, that you ever gave me birth'. Prophets are human.

18.title: At the Potter's House
18.context: At the potter's house — God has the right to reshape nations according to his purpose.

20.title: Jeremiah Persecuted
20.context: Jeremiah persecuted — beaten, locked in stocks. He even laments his calling.

23.title: Woe to the Shepherds
23.context: Woe to the shepherds — like Ezekiel 34, God promises a true Shepherd to come.

25.title: Seventy Years
25.context: Seventy years prophesied — Daniel later prays based on this text for Israel's return.

29.title: Letter to the Exiles
29.context: Letter to the exiles — including 'I know the plans I have for you'. One of the most-quoted promises in Scripture.

31.title: The New Covenant
31.context: The new covenant prophecy. Hebrews 8 quotes it in full, declaring it fulfilled in Christ — the law written on the heart, sin remembered no more.

32.title: Jeremiah Buys a Field
32.context: Jeremiah buys a field — in the besieged city. A prophetic sign that the people will return.

36.title: The Scroll Burned
36.context: The scroll burned — King Jehoiakim cuts and burns God's word. Yet the word survives and is rewritten.

37.title: Jeremiah Imprisoned
37.context: Jeremiah imprisoned — repeatedly. The prophet's cost.

38.title: Jeremiah Cast into a Cistern
38.context: Cast into a cistern — sinking into mud, almost dying. Saved by an Ethiopian eunuch.

39.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
39.context: The fall of Jerusalem — every prophecy Jeremiah preached for 40 years comes true.

40.title: Gedaliah Appointed
40.context: Gedaliah appointed — Babylon's puppet governor. A brief stability that won't last.

44.title: Jews in Egypt Rebuked
44.context: Jews in Egypt rebuked — survivors flee but resume idolatry. Sin is stubborn.

50.title: Prophecy Against Babylon
50.context: Prophecy against Babylon — even the conqueror will be conquered. God judges all.

52.title: Jerusalem Falls Reviewed
52.context: Jerusalem falls reviewed — the book ends with tragedy, but the promise of return remains.

1.title: How Lonely Sits the City
1.context: How lonely sits the city — 'Once full of people, now deserted'. A great city laid waste.

2.title: The LORD's Anger
2.context: The LORD's anger — God is the judge, and the hand that struck. A hard truth to face.

3.title: Affliction and Hope
3.context: 'I am the man who has seen affliction' — Jeremiah's personal voice for national grief.

3.title: His Mercies Are New
3.context: At the heart of the city's grief stands one of Scripture's greatest declarations of grace: 'His mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning.'

4.title: Horrors of the Siege
4.context: Horrors of the siege — mothers cooking their children; gold tarnished. The darkest pages.

5.title: Restore Us, O LORD
5.context: 'Restore us, O LORD' — the book ends without resolution. The unanswered question of every grief.

1.title: The Vision of God's Glory
1.context: The vision of God's glory — one of the most spectacular visions in Scripture. God reigns even in exile.

2.title: Ezekiel Called
2.context: Ezekiel called — 'Son of man'. God uses this title 93 times throughout the book.

3.title: The Watchman
3.context: The watchman — if you don't warn the wicked, their blood is on your head. A heavy charge.

4.title: Acted Prophecies
4.context: Acted prophecies — Ezekiel performs Jerusalem's siege. Visual sermons in the streets.

8.title: Abominations in the Temple
8.context: Abominations in the temple — Ezekiel is shown priests worshipping idols in the temple's hidden chambers.

10.title: God's Glory Departs
10.context: God's glory departs the temple — slow, sorrowful. 'Ichabod' — the glory is gone.

16.title: Unfaithful Jerusalem
16.context: Unfaithful Jerusalem — God's relationship with his people described as a deeply unfaithful marriage.

18.title: The Soul That Sins
18.context: The soul that sins — 'The one who sins is the one who will die'. A foundational text on individual responsibility.

24.title: Ezekiel's Wife Dies
24.context: Ezekiel's wife dies — and God forbids him to mourn, as a sign of the temple's destruction without lament.

25.title: Prophecies Against the Nations
25.context: Prophecies against the nations — Edom, Moab, Tyre, etc. God judges every people, not just Israel.

33.title: The Watchman Again
33.context: The watchman again — judgment has fallen. The call now becomes 'turn back, return!'

34.title: Shepherds of Israel
34.context: Shepherds rebuked — 'I myself will tend my sheep'. A direct preview of Christ the Good Shepherd.

36.title: A New Heart
36.context: 'I will give you a new heart… I will put my Spirit within you.' The Old Testament's clearest preview of Pentecost — and the heart of New Covenant living.

37.title: The Valley of Dry Bones
37.context: The valley of dry bones — can a destroyed nation live again? God's answer: yes, by my Word and my Spirit. The image still speaks today.

38.title: Gog and Magog
38.context: Gog and Magog — apocalyptic vision. Revelation 20 echoes this for the final battle.

40.title: The New Temple Vision
40.context: The new temple vision — vast and detailed. Many read it as the millennial temple.

47.title: Water from the Temple
47.context: Water from the temple — a deepening river that brings the Dead Sea to life. Revelation 22 picks up this image.

48.title: Land Allotments
48.context: Land allotments — the book closes naming the city 'The LORD Is There'. The deepest hope of all.

1.title: Daniel's Training in Babylon
1.context: Daniel's training — young men in a foreign court, names and culture changed, yet they refuse to be defiled.

2.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream
2.context: Nebuchadnezzar's dream — four kingdoms in a single image. God reveals the shape of history.

3.title: The Fiery Furnace
3.context: Three young men refuse to bow to a golden image. Their faith reads 'God can save us — but even if he does not, we will not bow.' One of Scripture's bravest moments.

4.title: Nebuchadnezzar Humbled
4.context: Nebuchadnezzar humbled — the proudest king becomes like a beast for seven years, then repents.

5.title: The Writing on the Wall
5.context: The writing on the wall — 'Mene, Mene, Tekel, Parsin'. An empire falls in a single night.

6.title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
6.context: Daniel in the lions' den — already an old man, still praying three times a day toward Jerusalem. Loyalty over self-preservation.

7.title: Vision of the Four Beasts
7.context: 'One like a son of man' coming on the clouds — Daniel's deepest preview of Christ. Jesus' favorite self-designation comes straight from this vision.

8.title: The Ram and the Goat
8.context: The ram and the goat — prophesying Persia's and Greece's rise. Alexander the Great foreseen.

9.title: Daniel's Prayer and the Seventy Sevens
9.context: Daniel reads Jeremiah's prophecy and his prayer awakens. This prophet teaches us how to pray Scripture's promises back to God.

10.title: The Final Vision Begins
10.context: The final vision begins — after three weeks of fasting for Israel, Daniel receives the climactic revelations.

11.title: Kings of the South and North
11.context: Kings of the south and north — detailed prophecies of Ptolemaic and Seleucid empires.

12.title: The End of Days
12.context: The end of days — 'Many who sleep in the dust will awake'. One of the OT's clearest resurrection prophecies.

1.title: Hosea's Marriage
1.context: Hosea's marriage — God commands him to marry an unfaithful woman as a living prophecy.

2.title: Israel's Adultery
2.context: Israel's adultery — yet God promises to speak tenderly to her in the wilderness, winning her back.

3.title: Hosea Redeems His Wife
3.context: Hosea redeems his wife — the core of his message and a foreshadow of Christ redeeming the church.

4.title: Without Knowledge
4.context: Without knowledge — 'My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge'. Knowing God matters.

6.title: Return to the LORD
6.context: Return to the LORD — the people's own words: 'Come, let us return!' The repentance Hosea has been pleading for.

11.title: God's Love for Israel
11.context: 'Out of Egypt I called my son' — Matthew 2 sees this fulfilled in Jesus' flight to Egypt.

14.title: Repent and Be Restored
14.context: Return and be restored — 'Return, O Israel'. Grace after judgment.

1.title: The Locust Plague
1.context: The locust plague — a natural disaster becomes a window into spiritual reality.

2.title: The Day of the LORD
2.context: The Day of the LORD — judgment and hope held together.

2.title: The Spirit Poured Out
2.context: The Spirit poured out — Peter quotes this on Pentecost, proclaiming it fulfilled in the church.

3.title: Judgment on the Nations
3.context: Judgment on the nations — God's justice reaches every people.

1.title: Judgments on Surrounding Nations
1.context: Judgments on neighboring nations — and then to Israel itself. God plays no favorites.

2.title: Against Judah and Israel
2.context: Against Judah and Israel — 'For three sins, even for four, I will not relent'.

3.title: Israel's Privilege and Punishment
3.context: Israel's privilege and punishment — 'You only have I known'. Election is not exemption.

5.title: Seek the LORD and Live
5.context: Seek the LORD and live — hope remains, but only through repentance.

5.title: Let Justice Roll Down
5.context: Let justice roll down — 'I hate, I despise your festivals'. Without justice, even worship becomes hypocrisy.

7.title: Five Visions
7.context: Five visions — locusts, fire, plumb line, fruit, the altar. Judgment intensifies.

9.title: The Restoration of Israel
9.context: The restoration of Israel — even a book of judgment ends in hope. Acts 15 cites this.

1.title: Edom's Judgment
1.context: Edom's judgment — descendants of Esau. God's judgment never overlooks pride.

1.title: Zion's Deliverance
1.context: Zion's deliverance — the 21-verse book's final word: 'The kingdom shall be the LORD's'.

1.title: Jonah Flees
1.context: Jonah doesn't flee the mission — he flees God's mercy. He doesn't want Nineveh to repent. Perhaps the Bible's most honest prophet.

1.title: In the Belly of the Fish
1.context: In the belly of the fish — Jesus calls this a foreshadow of his own resurrection (Matt 12:40).

2.title: Jonah's Prayer
2.context: Jonah's prayer — even from the depths, you can call on God.

3.title: Jonah Preaches in Nineveh
3.context: Nineveh repents — pagan Assyrians outdo God's own people in turning from sin. Jesus cites Jonah as a sign of his own resurrection (Matt 12:40).

4.title: Jonah's Anger and God's Mercy
4.context: Jonah's anger — he didn't want Nineveh repented. God patiently teaches him compassion.

1.title: Judgment Against Israel and Judah
1.context: Judgment on both kingdoms — Micah speaks to both north and south.

3.title: Leaders Rebuked
3.context: Leaders rebuked — when leaders fail, nations crumble.

4.title: The Mountain of the LORD
4.context: The mountain of the LORD — same vision as Isaiah 2: nations flowing to God's mountain.

5.title: A Ruler from Bethlehem
5.context: Under the shadow of exile, Micah names Bethlehem — the small town where the Messiah will be born. Cited in Matthew 2 to Herod's wise men.

6.title: What Does the LORD Require?
6.context: What does the LORD require? — Scripture's clearest summary of true religion: 'Do justice, love kindness, walk humbly with your God'.

7.title: Zion Restored
7.context: Zion restored — 'He delights to show mercy'. One of the deepest descriptions of God.

1.title: The LORD's Anger Against Nineveh
1.context: God's anger against Nineveh — mercy doesn't erase justice; justice doesn't erase mercy.

2.title: The Fall of Nineveh
2.context: The fall of Nineveh — a poem of war. God announces his judgment in verse.

3.title: Woe to Nineveh
3.context: Woe to Nineveh — 'Woe to the city of blood!' Oppressors will be judged.

1.title: Habakkuk's Complaint
1.context: Habakkuk's complaint — 'How long, LORD, must I call for help?' Honest doubt before God.

1.title: God's Answer
1.context: God's surprising answer — using one wicked nation to judge another. His ways are not ours.

2.title: The Righteous Live by Faith
2.context: 'The righteous shall live by his faith' — quoted three times in the New Testament. The seedbed of the Reformation's central doctrine.

3.title: Habakkuk's Prayer
3.context: Habakkuk's prayer — 'Though the fig tree does not bud… yet I will rejoice in the LORD'. Trust in the worst.

1.title: The Day of the LORD
1.context: The Day of the LORD — described in the harshest, most cosmic terms.

2.title: Judgment on the Nations
2.context: Judgment on the nations — Philistia, Moab, Ethiopia, Assyria.

3.title: Jerusalem's Doom and Restoration
3.context: Jerusalem's doom and restoration — followed by the stunning promise: 'He will rejoice over you with singing'.

1.title: The Call to Build
1.context: The call to build — 'Is it a time for you to live in paneled houses while this house lies in ruins?'

2.title: Glory of the New Temple
2.context: Glory of the new temple — 'The latter glory will surpass the former'. Fulfilled when Jesus walked into Herod's temple.

2.title: Promise to Zerubbabel
2.context: Promise to Zerubbabel — David's line preserved through exile. God's promises never fail.

1.title: Call to Return
1.context: Call to return — 'Return to me, says the LORD'. The shortest possible prophetic message.

1.title: Eight Night Visions
1.context: Eight night visions — God reveals his plans for history in a single night.

3.title: Joshua the High Priest
3.context: Joshua the high priest — Satan accuses, God clothes him in righteous robes. A foreshadow of what Christ does for believers.

4.title: The Lampstand Vision
4.context: The lampstand vision — 'Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD'.

8.title: Restoration of Zion
8.context: Restoration of Zion — old people with canes and children playing in the streets. A picture of peace.

9.title: The Coming King
9.context: 'Behold, your king comes… humble and riding on a donkey.' Prophesied 500 years before Palm Sunday — fulfilled to the letter in Matthew 21.

11.title: Two Shepherds
11.context: Two shepherds — thirty pieces of silver to betray the good shepherd. Matthew 27 sees this in Judas.

12.title: Looking Upon the Pierced One
12.context: 'They will look on me, the one they have pierced' — fulfilled in John 19 at the cross.

14.title: The Day of the LORD
14.context: The Day of the LORD — the Mount of Olives splits. Where Christ ascended is where he will return.

1.title: God's Love and Defiled Sacrifices
1.context: God's love and defiled sacrifices — 'How have you loved us?' The question that exposes spiritual deadness.

2.title: A Warning to the Priests
2.context: Warning to priests — 'You have caused many to stumble'. Spiritual leaders carry heavy responsibility.

2.title: Faithlessness in Marriage
2.context: Faithlessness in marriage — 'God hates divorce'. Marriage is covenant.

3.title: The Messenger Will Come
3.context: The messenger will come — John the Baptist prepares the way; the Lord himself comes to his temple.

3.title: Robbing God in Tithes
3.context: Robbing God in tithes — what we can withhold reveals what we love.

4.title: The Sun of Righteousness
4.context: The Old Testament's final prophecy: Elijah will come. John the Baptist fulfills it (Matt 11:14). Then 400 years of silence — until the angel speaks to Zechariah in Luke 1.

1.title: The Genealogy of Jesus
1.context: Matthew opens with a genealogy because identity matters. Jesus is shown to fulfill both the Abrahamic promise of blessing and the Davidic promise of an eternal King.

1.title: The Birth of Jesus
1.context: The birth of Jesus — a virgin, an obedient carpenter, a prophesied baby. The greatest story begins in the smallest home.

2.title: The Visit of the Magi
2.context: The Magi visit — Gentile wise men recognize the Messiah first. The gospel crossed ethnic lines from day one.

2.title: The Flight to Egypt
2.context: The flight to Egypt — the infant King is hunted from the start.

2.title: The Return to Nazareth
2.context: Return to Nazareth — fulfilling the prophecy 'He will be called a Nazarene'. God's providence at every step.

3.title: John the Baptist Prepares the Way
3.context: John the Baptist — 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near'. The doorway to the New Testament.

3.title: The Baptism of Jesus
3.context: Jesus' baptism — the Trinity appears together: Son in the water, Father speaking, Spirit descending.

4.title: The Temptation of Jesus
4.context: The temptation — 40 days. The Second Adam succeeds where the first failed.

4.title: Jesus Begins His Ministry
4.context: Ministry in Galilee — fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy: 'The people walking in darkness have seen a great light'.

4.title: Jesus Calls His First Disciples
4.context: Calling the first disciples — fishermen called to fish for people.

5.title: The Sermon on the Mount: The Beatitudes
5.context: Jesus' foundational sermon, delivered early in his Galilean ministry. The Beatitudes invert worldly values — calling the poor in spirit, the mourners, and the persecuted 'blessed'.

5.title: Salt and Light
5.context: Salt and light — Jesus' core declaration of disciple identity. Not a command but a statement of fact: you ARE these things; now live like it.

5.title: The Fulfillment of the Law
5.context: Jesus and the law — 'I have not come to abolish but to fulfill'. The bridge between Old and New.

5.title: Teaching About Anger
5.context: Teaching about anger — Jesus goes deeper: 'Anyone who is angry with a brother will be subject to judgment'. The law reaches the heart.

5.title: Teaching About Lust
5.context: Teaching about lust — 'Anyone who looks lustfully has already committed adultery'. God sees the heart, not just the action.

5.title: Teaching About Divorce
5.context: Teaching about divorce — protecting marriage's sanctity, restraining the casual divorces of his day.

5.title: Teaching About Oaths
5.context: Teaching about oaths — 'Let your yes be yes, your no be no'. Christian speech should be consistent.

5.title: Teaching About Retaliation
5.context: Teaching about retaliation — 'Do not resist an evil person'. Jesus begins a revolution against natural human instinct.

5.title: Love Your Enemies
5.context: Love your enemies — Jesus' most revolutionary teaching. 'That you may be sons of your Father in heaven'.

6.title: Teaching About Giving
6.context: Teaching about giving — not before people. God sees in secret, and rewards in secret.

6.title: Teaching About Prayer
6.context: Teaching about prayer — Jesus' fullest teaching on prayer. Quality over quantity.

6.title: The Lord's Prayer
6.context: The pattern Jesus gave his disciples for prayer. Every line is a window into the heart of how citizens of the kingdom relate to their Father.

6.title: Teaching About Fasting
6.context: Teaching about fasting — a hidden spiritual discipline, not for show.

6.title: Treasures in Heaven
6.context: Treasures in heaven — 'Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also'.

6.title: Do Not Worry
6.context: 'Do not be anxious' — Jesus says it three times. If your Father feeds the birds, will he not also feed you?

7.title: Do Not Judge
7.context: Do not judge — 'First take the plank out of your own eye'. Jesus teaches with humor and force.

7.title: Ask, Seek, Knock
7.context: Ask, seek, knock — 'Ask and it will be given'. The Father delights to hear his children pray.

7.title: The Narrow and Wide Gates
7.context: The narrow and wide gates — Jesus emphasizes that following him is a minority path.

7.title: True and False Prophets
7.context: True and false prophets — 'By their fruit you will recognize them'. Authenticity reveals itself over time.

7.title: The Wise and Foolish Builders
7.context: Wise and foolish builders — the climax of the Sermon: hearing matters less than doing.

8.title: Jesus Heals a Leper
8.context: Jesus heals a leper — touching the untouchable. Where Pharisees stand back, Jesus draws near.

8.title: The Faith of the Centurion
8.context: The centurion's faith — Jesus marvels: 'I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith'.

8.title: Jesus Heals Many
8.context: Jesus heals many — 'He bore our infirmities and carried our diseases'. Citing Isaiah 53.

8.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
8.context: Jesus calms the storm — the disciples' first encounter with Jesus' authority over nature.

8.title: The Demon-Possessed Men of Gadara
8.context: The Gadarene demoniacs — even demons recognize him as Son of God and fear his judgment.

9.title: Jesus Heals a Paralyzed Man
9.context: Jesus heals a paralytic — first forgiveness, then healing. The teachers of the law watch in shock.

9.title: The Calling of Matthew
9.context: Calling Matthew — a despised tax collector becomes a Gospel writer.

9.title: Question About Fasting
9.context: Question about fasting — 'How can the wedding guests mourn while the bridegroom is with them?'

9.title: The Dead Girl and the Sick Woman
9.context: Two desperate stories interlock — Jesus has time for both the prominent and the ostracized.

9.title: Jesus Heals the Blind and Mute
9.context: Jesus heals the blind and mute — 'Son of David!' — their cry is a confession of faith.

9.title: The Workers Are Few
9.context: The workers are few — Jesus' compassionate heart: 'They were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd'.

10.title: Jesus Sends Out the Twelve
10.context: Jesus sends out the Twelve — ministry multiplied. Authority shared with followers.

10.title: Coming Persecutions
10.context: Coming persecutions — Jesus predicts disciples will be hated, beaten, killed. 'For my name's sake'.

10.title: Acknowledging Christ
10.context: Acknowledging Christ — 'Whoever does not take up their cross is not worthy of me'.

11.title: Jesus and John the Baptist
11.context: John the Baptist's question — even a great prophet has moments of doubt in prison.

11.title: Woe to Unrepentant Cities
11.context: Woe and rest — 'Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened'.

12.title: The Lord of the Sabbath
12.context: Lord of the Sabbath — Jesus doesn't break the Sabbath but restores its purpose.

12.title: Jesus and Beelzebul
12.context: Jesus and Beelzebul — Pharisees accuse him of casting out demons by the prince of demons. Jesus' logical reply.

12.title: The Sign of Jonah
12.context: The sign of Jonah — Jesus tells the doubters: 'Three days and nights, just like Jonah'.

12.title: The True Family of Jesus
12.context: Jesus' true family — 'Whoever does the will of my Father is my brother and sister'.

13.title: The Parable of the Sower
13.context: The kingdom parables — Jesus reveals heavenly mysteries through earthly stories. Chapter 7 was the teacher; this chapter is the storyteller.

13.title: The Parable of the Weeds
13.context: The parable of the weeds — kingdom and world grow together until harvest.

13.title: The Mustard Seed and Yeast
13.context: Mustard seed and yeast — small beginnings, vast endings.

13.title: Hidden Treasure and Pearl
13.context: Hidden treasure and pearl — the kingdom is worth selling everything to obtain.

13.title: Rejected at Nazareth
13.context: Rejected at Nazareth — 'A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown'.

14.title: John the Baptist Beheaded
14.context: John the Baptist beheaded — a great prophet's tragic end. Herod's conscience haunts him.

14.title: Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand
14.context: After hearing of John the Baptist's death, Jesus withdraws — but the crowd follows. He feeds 5,000 with five loaves and two fish.

14.title: Jesus Walks on Water
14.context: Jesus walks on water — Peter steps out too, but sinks when his eyes leave Jesus.

15.title: Clean and Unclean
15.context: Tradition vs. command — Jesus distinguishes God's commands from human traditions.

15.title: The Faith of the Canaanite Woman
15.context: The Canaanite woman's faith — 'Even the dogs eat the crumbs from their master's table'.

15.title: Jesus Feeds the Four Thousand
15.context: Jesus feeds 4,000 — the second great feeding. His compassion overflows.

16.title: The Demand for a Sign
16.context: Demand for a sign — 'A wicked generation looks for a sign'. Jesus has already given dozens.

16.title: Peter's Confession of Christ
16.context: Peter's confession at Caesarea Philippi is the hinge of all four Gospels. After this moment, Jesus begins openly teaching that he must die and rise again.

16.title: Jesus Predicts His Death
16.context: Jesus predicts his death — Peter rebukes him. Jesus answers with the harshest word: 'Get behind me, Satan!'

17.title: The Transfiguration
17.context: On a mountain, Jesus' divine glory briefly breaks through his humanity. Moses (Law) and Elijah (Prophets) appear with him — both pointing to the One greater than themselves.

17.title: Jesus Heals a Demon-Possessed Boy
17.context: Healing a demon-possessed boy — disciples couldn't because 'this kind comes out only by prayer and fasting'.

17.title: The Temple Tax
17.context: The temple tax — Jesus pays with a coin from a fish's mouth. The Son of God submits to convention.

18.title: The Greatest in the Kingdom
18.context: The greatest in the kingdom — 'Unless you become like little children, you will not enter'.

18.title: The Parable of the Lost Sheep
18.context: The lost sheep — one strayer commands the shepherd's full attention. Heaven rejoices over one repenter.

18.title: Dealing with Sin in the Church
18.context: Dealing with sin in the church — Jesus' most practical teaching on church discipline.

18.title: The Parable of the Unforgiving Servant
18.context: The unforgiving servant — Peter asks 'seven times?' Jesus answers: 'seventy times seven'.

19.title: Jesus Teaches About Divorce
19.context: Jesus on divorce — returning to God's original Genesis design.

19.title: Jesus Blesses the Children
19.context: Jesus blesses the children — disciples push them away, Jesus welcomes them.

19.title: The Rich Young Ruler
19.context: The rich young ruler — 'Easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye'. One of Jesus' sharpest teachings.

20.title: The Workers in the Vineyard
20.context: Workers in the vineyard — same wage for one hour or twelve. God's grace is gloriously unfair.

20.title: Jesus Foretells His Death Again
20.context: Jesus foretells his death again — for the third time. He chooses the cross.

20.title: A Mother's Request
20.context: A mother's request — for top seats for her sons. Jesus redirects: 'Not so among you'.

20.title: Two Blind Men Receive Sight
20.context: Healing the blind — Bartimaeus. The blind see Jesus more clearly than the sighted.

21.title: The Triumphal Entry
21.context: Palm Sunday — Jesus enters Jerusalem riding a donkey, fulfilling Zechariah 9:9. A public declaration: I am the messianic King.

21.title: Jesus Cleanses the Temple
21.context: Cleansing the temple — Jesus does this twice. 'My house shall be a house of prayer, not a den of robbers'.

21.title: Jesus Curses the Fig Tree
21.context: Cursing the fig tree — a fruitless tree becomes a living prophecy of Israel's barren religion.

21.title: The Authority of Jesus Questioned
21.context: Authority questioned — Jesus answers with a question of his own about John the Baptist.

21.title: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants
21.context: The wicked tenants — Jesus publicly indicts the religious leaders. 'The kingdom will be taken from you'.

22.title: The Parable of the Wedding Banquet
22.context: The wedding banquet — many are invited, few are chosen.

22.title: Paying Taxes to Caesar
22.context: Paying taxes — 'Render to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's'. The most-cited political theology verse.

22.title: Marriage at the Resurrection
22.context: Marriage at the resurrection — Sadducees deny it. Jesus says God is 'the God of Abraham' — God of the living, not the dead.

22.title: The Greatest Commandment
22.context: The greatest commandment — love God and love neighbor. All the law and prophets.

23.title: Seven Woes to Religious Leaders
23.context: Seven woes — Jesus' sharpest words. Religious leaders who lead people astray face the strongest judgment.

24.title: Signs of the End of the Age
24.context: Signs of the end — the Olivet Discourse. Temple's destruction and the end of the age.

24.title: No One Knows the Day or Hour
24.context: No one knows the day — 'Not even the Son'. Christians watch but never predict.

25.title: The Parable of the Ten Virgins
25.context: Ten virgins — five wise, five foolish. Preparation is everything.

25.title: The Parable of the Talents
25.context: The talents — God invests, expects return. 'Well done, good and faithful servant'.

25.title: The Final Judgment
25.context: The final judgment — Jesus judges by how we treated 'the least of these.' Faith is real when it shows up at the side of the suffering.

26.title: The Plot Against Jesus
26.context: The plot against Jesus — religious leaders gather to scheme.

26.title: Jesus Anointed at Bethany
26.context: Anointed at Bethany — 'Wherever this gospel is preached, what she did will be told'.

26.title: Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus
26.context: Judas agrees to betray — thirty pieces of silver. Zechariah 11's prophecy fulfilled.

26.title: The Last Supper
26.context: Jesus' final Passover. By breaking bread and pouring the cup, he institutes the new covenant in his body and blood — a memorial the church keeps to this day.

26.title: Gethsemane
26.context: In Gethsemane, the fully human Jesus wrestles with the cup before him — and submits to the Father's will. The hour of redemption begins here.

26.title: Jesus Arrested
26.context: Jesus arrested — Judas' kiss. 'Friend, do what you came for'.

26.title: Jesus Before the Sanhedrin
26.context: Before the Sanhedrin — an illegal night trial.

26.title: Peter Disowns Jesus
26.context: Peter's denial — 'I don't know the man!' The most loyal disciple fails at the critical moment.

27.title: Judas Hangs Himself
27.context: Judas hangs himself — he knew he betrayed innocent blood. But he chose death over repentance.

27.title: Jesus Before Pilate
27.context: Before Pilate — the Roman governor finds no fault, yet condemns. Political cowardice.

27.title: The Soldiers Mock Jesus
27.context: The soldiers mock — the true King mocked by his subjects.

27.title: The Crucifixion
27.context: The crucifixion — the most public execution in history. The Gospels treat it with strange restraint, letting the event speak for itself.

27.title: The Death of Jesus
27.context: Jesus dies — 'It is finished!' The temple veil tears top to bottom. Access to God forever changed.

27.title: The Burial of Jesus
27.context: The burial of Jesus — Joseph of Arimathea, a wealthy secret disciple, finally goes public.

28.title: The Resurrection
28.context: The climax of the New Testament. The resurrection vindicates Jesus' atoning sacrifice and inaugurates the hope of eternal life for all who trust him.

28.title: The Report of the Guards
28.context: The guards' report — bribed to claim the disciples stole the body. The first anti-resurrection story.

28.title: The Great Commission
28.context: The Great Commission. The risen Jesus sends his disciples to all nations — the marching orders that have driven 2,000 years of Christian mission.

1.title: John the Baptist Prepares the Way
1.context: Mark moves at breakneck speed — the shortest, most action-packed Gospel. The opening line states the thesis: Jesus is the Son of God.

1.title: The Baptism of Jesus
1.context: Jesus' baptism — heaven torn open, Spirit descending, Father speaking. The Trinity together.

1.title: The Temptation of Jesus
1.context: The temptation — Mark covers 40 days in just two verses.

1.title: Jesus Begins His Ministry
1.context: Jesus begins his ministry — after John's arrest, Jesus comes out publicly.

1.title: Jesus Calls His First Disciples
1.context: Calling the first disciples — 'Come, follow me'. Ordinary fishermen called out.

1.title: Jesus Casts Out an Evil Spirit
1.context: Jesus casts out an evil spirit — 'What is this teaching with such authority?'

1.title: Jesus Heals Many
1.context: Healing Peter's mother-in-law — by sunset crowds gather. Jesus' ministry catches like fire.

1.title: Jesus Prays in a Solitary Place
1.context: Jesus prays alone — after the busiest day, he withdraws. A rhythm we desperately need.

1.title: Jesus Heals a Man with Leprosy
1.context: Jesus heals a leper — and touches him. The untouchable touched by holiness.

2.title: Jesus Heals a Paralyzed Man
2.context: Healing the paralytic — four friends tear off a roof. Jesus sees the friends' faith.

2.title: The Calling of Levi
2.context: Calling Levi — same as Matthew. Jesus specifically seeks the rejected.

2.title: Question About Fasting
2.context: Question about fasting — Jesus answers with new wine in new wineskins.

2.title: Lord of the Sabbath
2.context: Lord of the Sabbath — Jesus stands above the law, not under it.

3.title: Healing on the Sabbath
3.context: Healing on the Sabbath — Pharisees plot murder. Compassion becomes a crime.

3.title: Crowds Follow Jesus
3.context: Crowds follow Jesus — from every direction. His fame spreads far.

3.title: The Calling of the Twelve
3.context: Calling the Twelve — ordinary men chosen for the greatest mission in history.

3.title: Jesus and Beelzebul
3.context: Jesus and Beelzebul — his family thinks he's mad, the scribes say he's possessed. The pain of being misunderstood.

3.title: Jesus' True Family
3.context: Jesus' true family — 'Whoever does God's will is my brother'. Spiritual family transcends blood.

4.title: The Parable of the Sower
4.context: The sower — Jesus' most explained parable. Four types of hearts.

4.title: Lamp on a Stand
4.context: Lamp on a stand — 'With the measure you use, it will be measured to you'.

4.title: The Growing Seed
4.context: The growing seed — the farmer doesn't know how. The mystery of the kingdom.

4.title: The Mustard Seed
4.context: The mustard seed — smallest of all, becomes a tree. The kingdom starts small.

4.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
4.context: Jesus stills a storm. The terrified disciples ask the question Mark wants every reader to ask: 'Who is this, that even the wind and sea obey him?'

5.title: Jesus Restores the Demon-Possessed Man
5.context: The Gerasene demoniac — the townspeople ask Jesus to leave. Lost pigs disturb more than a delivered man.

5.title: A Dead Girl and a Sick Woman
5.context: Two desperate stories interlock: the synagogue ruler's daughter and the bleeding woman. Jesus has time for both — the prominent and the outcast.

6.title: A Prophet Without Honor
6.context: A prophet without honor — 'Only in his hometown is a prophet without honor'.

6.title: Jesus Sends Out the Twelve
6.context: Sending out the Twelve — two by two, with minimal supplies.

6.title: John the Baptist Beheaded
6.context: John the Baptist beheaded — Herod's conscience still troubles him long afterward.

6.title: Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand
6.context: Feeding the 5,000 — 'You give them something to eat'. Jesus makes impossibility into testimony.

6.title: Jesus Walks on Water
6.context: Jesus walks on water — the disciples cry out: 'It's a ghost!'

6.title: Healing the Sick in Gennesaret
6.context: Healing in Gennesaret — people line up the sick in the streets to touch his cloak.

7.title: Clean and Unclean
7.context: Tradition vs. command — Jesus' most direct critique.

7.title: The Faith of a Syrophoenician Woman
7.context: The Syrophoenician woman — a despised Gentile mother. Her faith moves Jesus.

7.title: Jesus Heals a Deaf and Mute Man
7.context: Healing a deaf and mute man — 'Ephphatha!' ('Be opened!').

8.title: Jesus Feeds the Four Thousand
8.context: Feeding the 4,000 — this time in Gentile territory. The kingdom's grace expanding.

8.title: The Yeast of the Pharisees
8.context: Demand for a sign — Pharisees keep testing. Jesus sighs and leaves.

8.title: Healing the Blind Man at Bethsaida
8.context: Healing in two stages — the only such miracle. Perhaps a parable of how faith grows in stages.

8.title: Peter's Confession of Christ
8.context: Mark's hinge. The first eight chapters answer 'Who is Jesus?' Peter's confession unlocks the second half: 'What did he come to do?' — to suffer and die.

8.title: Jesus Predicts His Death
8.context: First passion prediction — Peter rebukes Jesus. Jesus rebukes Peter: 'Get behind me, Satan!'

9.title: The Transfiguration
9.context: The Transfiguration — Jesus' divine glory breaks through, with Moses (Law) and Elijah (Prophets) appearing alongside. The veil lifts for one moment.

9.title: Jesus Heals a Boy with an Evil Spirit
9.context: Healing a possessed boy — the father's prayer: 'I believe; help my unbelief!'

9.title: Jesus Predicts His Death Again
9.context: Second passion prediction — they don't understand, and argue about who is greatest.

9.title: The Greatest in the Kingdom
9.context: Greatest in the kingdom — 'Whoever wants to be first must be last and servant of all'.

9.title: Whoever Is Not Against Us
9.context: Whoever causes a little one to stumble — 'Better a millstone tied around the neck'.

10.title: Jesus Teaches About Divorce
10.context: Jesus on divorce — back to the original design. 'The two shall become one'.

10.title: Jesus Blesses Little Children
10.context: Jesus blesses the children — 'The kingdom of God belongs to such as these'.

10.title: The Rich Young Man
10.context: The rich young man — 'One thing you lack'. Every heart has its 'one thing'.

10.title: Jesus Predicts His Death a Third Time
10.context: Third passion prediction — Jesus walks ahead; disciples follow in fear.

10.title: The Request of James and John
10.context: James and John's request — for glory seats. Jesus redirects to the only true leadership: service.

10.title: Blind Bartimaeus Receives Sight
10.context: Bartimaeus — his cry is a confession: 'Jesus, Son of David!' He sees more clearly than the seeing.

11.title: The Triumphal Entry
11.context: The triumphal entry — Jesus rides in on a donkey, fulfilling Zechariah 9:9.

11.title: Cursing the Fig Tree and Clearing the Temple
11.context: Cursing the fig tree and cleansing the temple — twin acts proclaiming: God will not accept outward religion.

11.title: The Authority of Jesus Questioned
11.context: Authority questioned — Jesus answers with a counter-question about John's baptism.

12.title: The Parable of the Tenants
12.context: The wicked tenants — the owner sends servants again and again, then his beloved son. They kill him.

12.title: Paying Taxes to Caesar
12.context: Paying taxes — 'Render to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's'.

12.title: Marriage at the Resurrection
12.context: Marriage at the resurrection — Sadducees deny it. Jesus answers: God is God of the living.

12.title: The Greatest Commandment
12.context: The greatest commandment — love God and neighbor. The summary of all the law and prophets.

12.title: The Widow's Offering
12.context: The widow's offering — two small coins outvalue every rich gift. God sees the heart, not the amount.

13.title: Signs of the End of the Age
13.context: Signs of the end — Mark's version of the Olivet Discourse.

13.title: The Day and Hour Unknown
13.context: No one knows the day — not even the Son. We watch and wait.

14.title: The Plot Against Jesus
14.context: The plot — religious leaders scheme to arrest and kill him.

14.title: Anointed at Bethany
14.context: Anointed at Bethany — 'Wherever the gospel is preached, what she has done will be told'.

14.title: The Last Supper
14.context: The Last Supper — Jesus institutes Communion. The church's 2,000-year remembrance.

14.title: Gethsemane
14.context: Gethsemane — Jesus' full humanity wrestles with the cup before him, but yields: 'Not my will, but yours be done.' The hour of redemption begins.

14.title: Jesus Arrested
14.context: Jesus arrested — 'Rabbi!' Judas uses an ordinary word to mark the greatest betrayal.

14.title: Before the Sanhedrin
14.context: Before the Sanhedrin — Jesus stays silent until directly asked if he is the Christ. He answers 'I am'.

14.title: Peter Disowns Jesus
14.context: Peter denies — 'I don't know him'. The most loyal disciple fails.

15.title: Jesus Before Pilate
15.context: Before Pilate — the Roman governor finds no fault.

15.title: The Soldiers Mock Jesus
15.context: The soldiers mock — pretending to honor the King who is the true King.

15.title: The Crucifixion
15.context: The crucifixion — Simon of Cyrene forced to carry the cross. His sons later become believers.

15.title: The Death of Jesus
15.context: Jesus' death — 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' The opening of Psalm 22.

15.title: The Burial of Jesus
15.context: The burial — Joseph of Arimathea takes the body. A secret disciple goes public.

16.title: Jesus Has Risen
16.context: The foundation of Christian faith. Mark's brief account is full of eyewitness texture — running, fear, breathlessness — the sound of life-altering news.

16.title: Jesus Appears to His Disciples
