16.context: Jesus appears — first to women, then to the apostles.

16.title: The Great Commission
16.context: The Great Commission — 'Go into all the world'. The church's 2,000-year mission.

1.title: Introduction to Theophilus
1.context: Luke writes to Theophilus — investigated carefully. The most historically careful Gospel.

1.title: John's Birth Foretold
1.context: John's birth foretold — old Zechariah goes mute for unbelief. God's promises never fail.

1.title: Jesus' Birth Foretold
1.context: Jesus' birth foretold — 'The Holy Spirit will come on you'. Mary's response: 'I am the Lord's servant'.

1.title: Mary Visits Elizabeth
1.context: Mary visits Elizabeth — baby John leaps in the womb. Two miraculous mothers meet.

1.title: Mary's Magnificat
1.context: Mary's Magnificat — 'My soul magnifies the Lord'. Echoing Hannah, a song of revolutionary hope.

1.title: The Birth of John
1.context: Birth of John — Zechariah's tongue is loosed in prophecy. The first New Testament canticle.

2.title: The Birth of Jesus
2.context: The birth of Jesus — in the middle of a Roman census, the Messiah is born outside a Bethlehem inn. God's story unfolds in real history.

2.title: Presentation in the Temple
2.context: Presentation in the temple — Simeon and Anna recognize 'God's salvation'.

2.title: Jesus at Twelve in the Temple
2.context: Jesus at twelve — 'Did you not know I had to be in my Father's house?' He already knows his mission.

3.title: John the Baptist Preaches
3.context: John's preaching — Luke anchors it in specific Roman dates. The Gospel is history.

3.title: The Baptism of Jesus
3.context: Jesus' baptism — 'You are my beloved Son'. The Father's affirmation.

3.title: The Genealogy of Jesus
3.context: Jesus' genealogy — Luke traces back to Adam. Jesus is 'Son of Man' connected to all humanity.

4.title: The Temptation
4.context: Jesus, baptized, is led into the wilderness — forty days mirroring Israel's forty years. The Second Adam succeeds where the first Israel failed.

4.title: Rejected at Nazareth
4.context: Rejected at Nazareth — after reading Isaiah 61, Jesus declares: 'Today this Scripture is fulfilled'.

4.title: Ministry in Capernaum
4.context: Ministry in Capernaum — 'They were amazed at his teaching'.

5.title: Calling the First Disciples
5.context: Calling the first disciples — Peter cries: 'Go away from me, Lord; I am a sinful man!'

5.title: Healing a Leper
5.context: Healing a leper — Jesus reaches out and touches him.

5.title: Healing the Paralytic
5.context: Healing the paralytic — four friends' faith. Jesus first forgives.

5.title: Calling Levi
5.context: Calling Levi — 'I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance'.

6.title: Choosing the Twelve
6.context: Choosing the Twelve — after a night of prayer.

6.title: The Sermon on the Plain
6.context: The Sermon on the Plain — Luke's version of the great sermon.

7.title: The Centurion's Servant
7.context: The centurion's servant — 'I have not seen such great faith in Israel'.

7.title: Widow's Son at Nain Raised
7.context: The widow's son raised — Jesus' compassion. 'Don't cry' is a Lucan signature.

7.title: The Sinful Woman Forgiven
7.context: The sinful woman forgiven — 'Her many sins have been forgiven, for she loved much'.

8.title: The Parable of the Sower
8.context: The sower — four hearts, four outcomes.

8.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
8.context: Jesus calms the storm — 'Master, we are perishing!' He rebukes the wind.

8.title: The Gerasene Demoniac
8.context: The Gerasene demoniac — a legion of demons sent into pigs.

9.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
9.context: Feeding the 5,000 — recorded in all four Gospels.

9.title: Peter's Confession
9.context: Peter's confession — 'God's Messiah'. Then Jesus speaks of taking up the cross.

9.title: The Transfiguration
9.context: The Transfiguration — Jesus' face altered. Moses and Elijah appear.

10.title: The Seventy Sent Out
10.context: The 72 sent out — expanded mission. 'The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few'.

10.title: The Good Samaritan
10.context: The Good Samaritan — Jesus shatters racial prejudice, redefining 'neighbor' as anyone in need. The hated foreigner becomes the hero.

10.title: Mary and Martha
10.context: Mary and Martha — service matters, but listening matters more. 'Mary has chosen what is better'.

11.title: Jesus Teaches About Prayer
11.context: Teaching about prayer — 'Lord, teach us to pray'. Jesus gives the Lord's Prayer.

12.title: The Rich Fool
12.context: The rich fool — 'Soul, you have plenty of goods'. Then God says: 'You fool!'

13.title: Parables of the Kingdom
13.context: Parables of the kingdom — mustard seed, yeast. Small beginnings, vast endings.

14.title: The Great Banquet
14.context: The great banquet — invited guests make excuses. So the host invites the poor and lame.

15.title: Lost and Found
15.context: Three parables of lost things found — sheep, coin, son. Each shows God actively seeking and joyfully receiving. The heart of the gospel in story form.

16.title: Two Stewards Parables
16.context: Two parables on stewardship — 'You cannot serve both God and money'.

17.title: Ten Lepers
17.context: Ten lepers — only one returns to thank, and he is a Samaritan.

18.title: Two Parables on Prayer
18.context: Two parables on prayer — 'All who exalt themselves will be humbled'.

18.title: Healing the Blind Beggar
18.context: Healing the blind beggar — calls Jesus 'Son of David'. His spiritual eyes opened first.

19.title: Zacchaeus
19.context: Zacchaeus — chief tax collector of Jericho, despised by all. Jesus invites himself to dinner. 'The Son of Man came to seek and save the lost.'

19.title: The Parable of the Minas
19.context: The parable of the minas — Jesus predicts he will leave and return. Servants must steward faithfully.

19.title: The Triumphal Entry
19.context: The triumphal entry — even if these were silent, the stones would cry out.

19.title: Cleansing the Temple
19.context: Cleansing the temple — 'My house is to be a house of prayer'. Jesus' anger at religious corruption.

22.title: The Last Supper
22.context: The Last Supper — Jesus institutes Communion. 'This is my body, given for you'.

22.title: Gethsemane and Arrest
22.context: Gethsemane and arrest — 'Not my will, but yours'.

22.title: Peter's Denial
22.context: Peter's denial — 'I don't know him'. The rooster crows. Jesus turns and looks at Peter.

23.title: Before Pilate and Herod
23.context: Before Pilate and Herod — Pilate declares him innocent three times, then condemns him.

23.title: The Crucifixion
23.context: The crucifixion — 'Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they're doing'.

23.title: Burial of Jesus
23.context: The burial — Joseph of Arimathea, a Sanhedrin member who opposed the verdict.

24.title: The Resurrection
24.context: The Resurrection — women arrive at dawn, meet two angels. The foundation of Christian faith.

24.title: On the Road to Emmaus
24.context: On the road to Emmaus — two discouraged disciples meet the risen Christ, who shows them how all of Scripture points to himself.

24.title: Jesus Appears to the Disciples
24.context: Jesus appears — comes among them. 'Peace be with you'.

24.title: The Ascension
24.context: The Ascension — Jesus blesses them at Bethany and is taken up. The earthly ministry ends.

1.title: The Word Became Flesh
1.context: John mirrors Genesis with his opening: 'In the beginning was the Word.' The eternal Logos — through whom all things were made — has now become flesh.

1.title: John the Baptist's Testimony
1.context: John's testimony — 'I am not the Christ, but his forerunner'.

1.title: The First Disciples Follow Jesus
1.context: The first disciples — Andrew comes first, then brings his brother Peter.

1.title: Jesus Calls Philip and Nathanael
1.context: Calling Philip and Nathanael — 'Come and see'. The simplest evangelism.

2.title: The Wedding at Cana
2.context: The wedding at Cana — Jesus' first sign. Water into wine. The new covenant has begun.

2.title: Jesus Clears the Temple
2.context: Cleansing the temple — early in his ministry. The temple must be a place of worship.

3.title: Jesus Teaches Nicodemus
3.context: A leading Pharisee comes by night for an encounter that contains the most-quoted verse in the Bible (3:16) — and a teaching that has changed millions of lives.

3.title: John Testifies Again About Jesus
3.context: John testifies again — 'He must increase, I must decrease'. The highest pattern of spiritual leadership.

4.title: The Samaritan Woman at the Well
4.context: Jesus crosses every boundary — racial, gender, religious — to offer 'living water' to a Samaritan woman at a well. By chapter's end, her village believes.

4.title: The Disciples Rejoin Jesus
4.context: The harvest is ready — 'Open your eyes and look at the fields! They are ripe for harvest'.

4.title: Jesus Heals an Official's Son
4.context: Healing an official's son — Jesus' word heals at a distance.

5.title: Healing at the Pool
5.context: Healing at the pool — a man sick 38 years. Then religious leaders accuse Jesus of Sabbath-breaking.

5.title: Life Through the Son
5.context: Life through the Son — Jesus' clearest declarations of his deity.

6.title: Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand
6.context: Feeding the 5,000 — the only miracle (besides the resurrection) recorded in all four Gospels. John uses it to open the 'I am the bread of life' discourse.

6.title: Jesus Walks on Water
6.context: Jesus walks on water — at night, in a storm. He comes to them across the waves.

6.title: Jesus the Bread of Life
6.context: Bread of life — 'I am the bread of life'. The spiritual interpretation of feeding the 5,000.

6.title: Many Disciples Desert Jesus
6.context: Many disciples desert — 'This is a hard teaching'. Peter answers: 'Lord, to whom shall we go?'

7.title: Jesus Goes to the Festival
7.context: Jesus goes to the festival — his own brothers don't believe in him.

7.title: Is Jesus the Messiah?
7.context: Is Jesus the Messiah? — the crowd is divided.

7.title: Streams of Living Water
7.context: Streams of living water — 'If anyone is thirsty, let them come to me and drink'.

8.title: The Woman Caught in Adultery
8.context: The woman caught in adultery — 'Let any one of you who is without sin cast the first stone.' One of Jesus' most famous defenses of mercy.

8.title: Jesus the Light of the World
8.context: Light of the world — 'I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness'.

8.title: The Truth Will Set You Free
8.context: The truth will set you free — only those who hold to Jesus' teaching are truly free.

9.title: Jesus Heals a Man Born Blind
9.context: A man born blind sees — but the climax is not physical sight but spiritual vision. 'Lord, I believe.' Both eyes finally open.

10.title: The Good Shepherd
10.context: 'I am the good shepherd' — Jesus echoes Ezekiel 34's rebuke of failed shepherds and steps into the role himself. The Lord is my shepherd.

10.title: Further Conflict
10.context: Further conflict — 'I and the Father are one'. They pick up stones to kill him.

11.title: The Death and Raising of Lazarus
11.context: The most dramatic miracle in John's Gospel. Raising Lazarus — dead four days — both ignites Jesus' final week and previews his own resurrection.

11.title: The Plot to Kill Jesus
11.context: The plot to kill Jesus — Lazarus' resurrection becomes the trigger for Jesus' death.

12.title: Jesus Anointed at Bethany
12.context: Anointed at Bethany — Mary prepares him for burial.

12.title: The Triumphal Entry
12.context: The triumphal entry — 'Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!'

12.title: Jesus Predicts His Death
12.context: Jesus predicts his death — 'When I am lifted up, I will draw all people to myself'.

13.title: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
13.context: On the night of his betrayal, the King washes his disciples' feet — overturning every worldly notion of power and service in a single act.

13.title: Jesus Predicts His Betrayal
13.context: Jesus predicts his betrayal — handing the bread to Judas. Mercy until the last moment.

13.title: Jesus Predicts Peter's Denial
13.context: A new command — 'Love one another'. The defining mark of Jesus' followers.

14.title: I Am the Way, Truth, and Life
14.context: On the night of his betrayal, Jesus comforts his frightened disciples: 'I am the way, the truth, and the life.' Words still anchoring believers today.

14.title: The Promise of the Holy Spirit
14.context: Promise of the Spirit — 'Another Helper'. The promise of Pentecost.

15.title: The True Vine
15.context: 'I am the true vine' — Jesus uses Israel's classic self-image to describe the life-union between himself and his followers.

15.title: The World Hates the Disciples
15.context: The world hates the disciples — 'If the world hates you, know that it hated me first'.

16.title: The Work of the Holy Spirit
16.context: The Spirit's work — convicting the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment.

16.title: The Disciples' Grief Will Turn to Joy
16.context: The disciples' grief will turn to joy — like a woman in labor: pain, then joy.

17.title: Jesus Prays for Himself and His Disciples
17.context: Jesus' high priestly prayer — interceding for his disciples and for every believer who would come after them. The deepest prayer in the New Testament.

18.title: Jesus Arrested
18.context: Jesus arrested — he goes out to meet them. 'Who do you seek?'

18.title: Peter Denies Jesus
18.context: Peter's denial — he claims to follow but denies three times.

18.title: Jesus Before Pilate
18.context: Before Pilate — 'My kingdom is not of this world'. Jesus clarifies his kingdom.

19.title: Jesus Sentenced to Be Crucified
19.context: Jesus sentenced — Pilate declares him innocent thrice, then bows to the crowd.

19.title: The Crucifixion
19.context: The crucifixion — 'It is finished!' Not a cry of defeat, but of triumph.

19.title: The Burial of Jesus
19.context: The burial — Joseph and Nicodemus, two secret disciples, finally go public.

20.title: The Empty Tomb
20.context: The empty tomb — the foundation of the Christian faith. John records the details of what he himself saw with the precision of an eyewitness.

20.title: Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene
20.context: Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene — 'Mary'. One word, and the greatest joy floods in.

20.title: Jesus Appears to His Disciples
20.context: Jesus appears to his disciples — 'Peace be with you'. His first post-resurrection word is peace.

20.title: Jesus Appears to Thomas
20.context: Doubting Thomas — 'Unless I see…'. A week later, Jesus appears just for him.

21.title: Jesus and the Miraculous Catch of Fish
21.context: By the Sea of Tiberias — empty nets all night. Jesus' word: cast on the right side. 153 fish.

21.title: Jesus Reinstates Peter
21.context: Peter restored — three denials, three questions, three restorations. 'Feed my sheep'.

1.title: Prologue and Promise of the Spirit
1.context: Luke continues the story: the risen Jesus appears for forty days and tells the apostles to wait for the promised Spirit.

1.title: The Ascension
1.context: On the Mount of Olives Jesus is taken up; two angels promise he will come back the same way.

1.title: Matthias Replaces Judas
1.context: About 120 disciples gather and cast lots, choosing Matthias to complete the Twelve.

2.title: Pentecost: The Spirit Comes
2.context: A sound like wind and tongues like fire fall on the disciples, who speak the wonders of God in many languages.

2.title: Peter Preaches at Pentecost
2.context: Peter cites David to argue Jesus’ resurrection and enthronement: God has made him both Lord and Christ.

2.title: Three Thousand Baptised
2.context: “What shall we do?” the crowd asks, cut to the heart; about three thousand are added that day.

2.title: Life of the First Believers
2.context: Sharing all things, breaking bread, daily prayer — the earliest portrait of the church.

3.title: The Lame Man at the Beautiful Gate
3.context: Peter and John heal a man lame from birth in the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

3.title: Peter at Solomon’s Portico
3.context: Peter tells the gathered crowd: the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob has glorified his servant Jesus.

4.title: Peter and John Arrested
4.context: The Sadducees, troubled by the resurrection message, jail the apostles overnight.

4.title: Before the Sanhedrin
4.context: Filled with the Spirit, Peter declares: there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved.

4.title: The Believers Pray for Boldness
4.context: Released, the apostles return to their own and the whole gathering lifts one voice in prayer.

4.title: All Things in Common
4.context: Of one heart and soul; no one claims any of his possessions as his own.

5.title: Ananias and Sapphira
5.context: Husband and wife lie to the Spirit; both fall dead in turn, and great fear seizes the church.

5.title: Apostles Heal the Sick
5.context: Crowds bring the sick into the streets so that Peter’s shadow might fall on them.

5.title: Apostles Freed by an Angel
5.context: Locked in jail, the apostles are released by an angel and told to keep teaching in the temple.

5.title: Gamaliel’s Counsel
5.context: The Pharisee Gamaliel warns: if this is from God you cannot stop them.

6.title: Seven Deacons Appointed
6.context: Seven men are set apart to oversee daily distribution so the apostles can devote themselves to prayer and the word.

6.title: Stephen Accused
6.context: Stephen, full of grace and power, is dragged before the council on false charges.

7.title: Stephen’s Speech
7.context: From Abraham to Solomon: Israel has always resisted the messengers God sent.

7.title: Stephen Martyred
7.context: The crowd stops their ears, drives him out and stones him; Saul stands by approving.

8.title: The Church Scattered
8.context: Persecution drives the Jerusalem believers throughout Judea and Samaria.

8.title: Philip in Samaria
8.context: Philip preaches Christ in a Samaritan city; unclean spirits come out and the lame walk.

8.title: Simon the Magician
8.context: Simon offers money for the power to confer the Spirit and is rebuked sharply by Peter.

8.title: The Ethiopian Eunuch
8.context: Philip explains Isaiah 53 to a court official on the road; the eunuch is baptised on the spot.

9.title: Saul on the Damascus Road
9.context: A blinding light, a voice from heaven; the persecutor falls to the ground.

9.title: Ananias Prays for Saul
9.context: A reluctant disciple lays hands on Saul; sight returns and the Spirit fills him.

9.title: Saul Begins to Preach
9.context: In Damascus synagogues he proclaims Jesus is the Son of God; a plot arises against his life.

9.title: Barnabas Welcomes Saul
9.context: When Jerusalem disciples are afraid, Barnabas brings Saul to the apostles and tells what happened.

9.title: Peter Heals Aeneas
9.context: In Lydda Peter says: Jesus Christ heals you. Aeneas rises immediately.

9.title: Tabitha Raised
9.context: In Joppa Peter prays alone and tells the dead Tabitha to get up; she opens her eyes.

10.title: Cornelius’s Vision
10.context: A devout Roman centurion in Caesarea sees an angel at three in the afternoon; he sends for Peter.

10.title: Peter’s Vision of the Sheet
10.context: Praying on the rooftop, Peter sees the same vision three times: do not call unclean what God has cleansed.

10.title: Peter Visits Cornelius
10.context: To Cornelius’s gathered household Peter declares: God shows no partiality.

10.title: The Spirit Falls on Gentiles
10.context: Peter is still speaking when the Spirit comes on every listener; they speak in tongues and praise God.

11.title: Peter Reports to Jerusalem
11.context: The circumcision party challenges Peter for eating with Gentiles; he recounts what God has done.

11.title: The Antioch Church
11.context: Disciples are first called Christians at Antioch; Barnabas brings Saul from Tarsus to teach for a year.

11.title: Agabus Foretells Famine
11.context: A prophet predicts famine across the Roman world; the believers send relief to Judea.

12.title: James Killed, Peter Imprisoned
12.context: Herod beheads James and arrests Peter, planning a public trial after Passover.

12.title: An Angel Frees Peter
12.context: While the church prays, an angel strikes Peter, leads him out, and the iron gate opens by itself.

12.title: The Death of Herod
12.context: Robed and enthroned, Herod accepts worship; an angel strikes him down and he is eaten by worms.

13.title: Antioch Sends Out Missionaries
13.context: The Spirit speaks during fasting and prayer: set apart Barnabas and Saul for the work.

13.title: In Cyprus
13.context: In Paphos Saul (now called Paul) rebukes the magician Elymas; the proconsul Sergius Paulus believes.

13.title: In Pisidian Antioch
13.context: Paul preaches Israel’s history in the synagogue and proclaims Jesus as David’s promised Saviour.

13.title: Turning to the Gentiles
13.context: Rejected by the Jews of the city, Paul declares boldly: we now turn to the Gentiles.

14.title: In Iconium
14.context: Paul and Barnabas speak boldly in the synagogue; God grants signs and wonders through their hands.

14.title: In Lystra
14.context: After healing a man lame from birth, the crowd tries to sacrifice to them; later Paul is stoned and left for dead.

14.title: Return to Antioch
14.context: Strengthening disciples and appointing elders, they report how God opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

15.title: The Jerusalem Council
15.context: Whether Gentile believers must be circumcised — apostles and elders gather to decide.

15.title: The Council’s Letter
15.context: A decree goes out: do not lay this burden on Gentile disciples; only abstain from a few essentials.

15.title: Paul and Barnabas Part Ways
15.context: A sharp disagreement over John Mark sends them in opposite directions; Paul takes Silas.

16.title: Timothy Joins Paul
16.context: In Lystra Paul circumcises Timothy because of the local Jews and takes him along.

16.title: The Macedonian Vision
16.context: A man pleads at night: come over to Macedonia and help us; Paul leaves immediately for Europe.

16.title: Lydia in Philippi
16.context: At a riverside prayer place the Lord opens the heart of Lydia, a seller of purple cloth; her household is baptised.

16.title: The Slave Girl Exorcised
16.context: Paul commands a fortune-telling spirit to leave; her owners stir up the city in revenge.

16.title: The Philippian Jailer
16.context: Midnight singing and prayer, an earthquake, a jailer’s entire household believing and being baptised.

17.title: In Thessalonica
17.context: For three Sabbaths Paul reasons in the synagogue that Jesus is the Messiah; jealous Jews stir a riot.

17.title: In Berea
17.context: The Bereans search the Scriptures daily to verify the message — more noble than the Thessalonians.

17.title: Paul Waits in Athens
17.context: Distressed by the city’s idols, Paul argues every day in the synagogue and the marketplace.

17.title: Sermon on the Areopagus
17.context: Beginning from “the unknown god,” Paul proclaims the Creator, repentance, resurrection and judgement.

18.title: Paul in Corinth
18.context: Working alongside Aquila and Priscilla; the Lord speaks at night: do not be afraid, keep speaking.

18.title: Return to Antioch
18.context: After eighteen months Paul cuts his hair, sails back, and rests at the home church.

18.title: Apollos in Ephesus
18.context: A fervent Apollos knows only John’s baptism; Priscilla and Aquila explain the way of God more accurately.

19.title: Paul in Ephesus
19.context: Paul finds twelve disciples in Ephesus who knew only John's baptism, and baptises them in the name of Jesus.

19.title: The Hall of Tyrannus
19.context: After three months in the synagogue Paul moves to the lecture hall of Tyrannus and reasons there daily for two years.

19.title: Extraordinary Miracles
19.context: God works unusual miracles through Paul’s hands; even handkerchiefs touched to him heal the sick.

19.title: The Sons of Sceva
19.context: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, try to invoke Jesus’ name to drive out an evil spirit and are overpowered.

19.title: Burning of Magic Books
19.context: Believers confess and bring their sorcery scrolls together to burn publicly — fifty thousand pieces of silver in value.

19.title: The Riot of the Silversmiths
19.context: Demetrius, a silversmith, stirs up Ephesus against Paul over the loss of his Artemis idol trade.

20.title: Through Macedonia and Greece
20.context: After three months in Greece, a plot against Paul sends him back through Macedonia.

20.title: Eutychus at Troas
20.context: A young man falls from a third-storey window during a long sermon; Paul embraces him and he revives.

20.title: Farewell to the Ephesian Elders
20.context: At Miletus Paul charges them: the Spirit has made you overseers — keep watch over yourselves and the flock.

21.title: Toward Jerusalem
21.context: From Miletus through Tyre and Caesarea, prophets warn Paul of bonds; he goes on resolute.

21.title: Arrival in Jerusalem
21.context: James and the elders advise Paul to take part in a purification rite with four men under a vow.

21.title: Arrest in the Temple
21.context: Asian Jews stir the crowd; the whole city is in uproar and the tribune rescues Paul.

22.title: Paul’s Defence
22.context: In Hebrew Paul recounts his Pharisee training and his encounter on the road to Damascus.

22.title: Paul’s Roman Citizenship
22.context: About to be flogged, Paul reveals he was born a Roman citizen; the tribune is shaken.

22.title: Before the Sanhedrin
22.context: The next day the tribune brings Paul down to stand before the chief priests and the council.

23.title: Defence Before the Sanhedrin
23.context: Seeing the council split between Sadducees and Pharisees, Paul shouts about the resurrection of the dead.

23.title: The Lord Appears at Night
23.context: The Lord stands by Paul: take courage; as you have testified at Jerusalem, so you must testify at Rome.

23.title: A Plot to Kill Paul
23.context: Forty men vow not to eat or drink until Paul is dead; his nephew tells the tribune.

23.title: Sent to Caesarea
23.context: That night the tribune dispatches 200 soldiers and 70 cavalry to escort Paul to the governor Felix.

24.title: Tertullus Accuses Paul
24.context: High priest Ananias and the orator Tertullus charge Paul as ringleader of the Nazarene sect.

24.title: Paul Before Felix
24.context: Paul confesses to worshipping the God of his ancestors and hoping for the resurrection of the dead.

24.title: Two Years in Custody
24.context: Felix hopes for a bribe and keeps summoning Paul; after two years Festus succeeds him.

25.title: Festus Takes the Case
25.context: Paul appeals to Caesar; Festus declares: to Caesar you have appealed, to Caesar you shall go.

25.title: King Agrippa Visits
25.context: Agrippa and Bernice come to greet Festus; Festus lays Paul’s case before the king.

26.title: Defence Before Agrippa
26.context: Paul tells how he persecuted the church, met the risen Christ on the road, and now preaches repentance to the Gentiles.

26.title: Almost Persuaded
26.context: Agrippa: in a short time you would persuade me to be a Christian. Paul: short or long, I would all who hear me become as I am.

27.title: Setting Sail for Rome
27.context: Paul and the other prisoners are handed over to Julius the centurion and sail from Caesarea.

27.title: The Storm at Sea
27.context: A wind called Euraquilo sweeps down from the island; for many days no sun, no stars, and all hope is lost.

27.title: Hope for All on Board
27.context: Paul stands among them: God has given me all who sail with you; not one will be lost.

27.title: All Brought Safely Ashore
27.context: At dawn the ship strikes a reef; everyone reaches land swimming or on planks of wood.

28.title: On the Island of Malta
28.context: The islanders show unusual kindness; Paul shakes off a viper unharmed and heals Publius’s father.

28.title: Arrival in Rome
28.context: Through Sicily and the Italian coast to the Forum of Appius; brothers come to meet Paul, who thanks God.

28.title: Meeting the Jewish Leaders
28.context: Three days after arriving Paul calls the Jewish leaders together and explains his case.

28.title: Preaching the Kingdom Boldly
28.context: For two whole years in his rented quarters Paul welcomes all who come, proclaiming the kingdom of God with full boldness.

1.title: Greeting
1.context: Greeting — Paul's unusually long opening declaring his apostolic calling and the gospel's nature.

1.title: Paul's Longing to Visit Rome
1.context: Paul's longing — many attempts unsuccessful. God's plan has its own timing.

1.title: The Power of the Gospel
1.context: Paul's thesis: 'I am not ashamed of the Gospel — it is the power of God for salvation.' Everything in Romans unpacks this single sentence.

1.title: God's Wrath Against Mankind
1.context: God's wrath — 'revealed from heaven'. No one has any excuse.

2.title: God's Righteous Judgment
2.context: God's righteous judgment — 'God does not show favoritism'. Jew or Gentile, all must face him.

2.title: The Jews and the Law
2.context: The Jews and the law — hearing it doesn't justify, only doing it. But who does it perfectly?

3.title: The Faithfulness of God
3.context: What is Jewish advantage? — Paul anticipates the obvious objection.

3.title: No One Is Righteous
3.context: All under sin — a string of Old Testament quotes: 'No one is righteous, not even one'.

3.title: Righteousness Through Faith
3.context: The heart of Romans — and arguably the heart of the Gospel. God's righteousness is revealed apart from the law and received through faith in Christ alone.

4.title: Abraham Justified by Faith
4.context: Abraham justified by faith — Paul's argument: even the Old Testament's hero was justified by faith, not works.

4.title: The Promise Through Faith
4.context: The promise through faith — Abraham father of all who believe, Jew and Gentile.

5.title: Peace and Hope
5.context: The fruits of justification: peace with God, access to grace, hope, and the strange gift of suffering — which produces the very character we long for.

5.title: Adam and Christ
5.context: Adam and Christ — one man's sin, all become sinners. One man's righteousness, all are made righteous.

6.title: Dead to Sin, Alive in Christ
6.context: Dead to sin, alive in Christ — believers have died to sin. How can we still live in it?

6.title: Slaves to Righteousness
6.context: Slaves to righteousness — once slaves of sin, now slaves of righteousness.

7.title: Released from the Law
7.context: Released from the law — Christians are no longer bound by the law's condemnation.

7.title: The Law and Sin
7.context: The law and sin — the law is good; it reveals sin and leads us to Christ.

7.title: The Inner Conflict
7.context: The inner conflict — 'The good I want to do, I do not do'. Every honest believer has felt this.

8.title: Life Through the Spirit
8.context: One of the highest peaks in Scripture. 'No condemnation' opens the chapter; 'no separation' closes it. In between: the Spirit, suffering, and unshakable hope.

8.title: Future Glory
8.context: Future glory — 'The sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory'.

8.title: More Than Conquerors
8.context: All things work together — one of the most-cited promises: 'In all things God works for the good of those who love him'.

9.title: Paul's Sorrow for Israel
9.context: Paul's sorrow for Israel — 'I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish'. A soul that loves his people.

9.title: God's Sovereign Choice
9.context: God's sovereign choice — a difficult topic. Paul's answer: God is God, and we are not.

9.title: Israel's Unbelief
9.context: Israel's unbelief — pursuing law-righteousness, missing faith-righteousness.

10.title: Salvation by Faith for All
10.context: Salvation by faith — 'Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved'. The gospel's heart.

10.title: Faith Comes from Hearing
10.context: Faith comes from hearing — so missionaries must be sent. The biblical foundation for missions.

11.title: The Remnant of Israel
11.context: The remnant of Israel — God has not rejected his people. Never.

11.title: Ingrafted Branches
11.context: Gentile branches grafted in — but never with arrogance over the natural branches.

11.title: All Israel Will Be Saved
11.context: All Israel will be saved — Paul foresees Israel's eventual return to Christ. God's promises stand.

11.title: Doxology
11.context: Doxology — 'How unsearchable his judgments, and his paths beyond tracing out!'

12.title: A Living Sacrifice
12.context: The pivot from doctrine to ethics. In view of God's mercy, we offer ourselves as living sacrifices — and the rest of life flows from that response.

12.title: Love in Action
12.context: Love in action — 'Love must be sincere'. Practical instruction on living Christ's love.

13.title: Submission to Authorities
13.context: Submission to authorities — all governing power is established by God.

13.title: Love Fulfills the Law
13.context: Love fulfills the law — 'Owe no one anything, except to love one another'.

13.title: The Day Is Near
13.context: The day is near — wake from sleep, put on Christ.

14.title: The Weak and the Strong
14.context: The weak and the strong — think of your weaker brother's conscience; don't trip them up.

14.title: Do Not Cause to Stumble
14.context: Do not cause to stumble — meat isn't worth a brother's faith.

15.title: Pleasing Others, Not Ourselves
15.context: Pleasing others — Christians don't live for themselves but for the good of others.

15.title: Paul's Apostolic Ministry
15.context: Paul's apostolic ministry — his unique calling: to bring the gospel to the Gentiles.

15.title: Paul's Plan to Visit Rome
15.context: Paul's plan — Rome first, then Spain. The mission keeps moving outward.

16.title: Personal Greetings
16.context: Personal greetings — a list of names: women, Gentiles, slaves. The gospel truly is for all.

16.title: Final Warning
16.context: Final warning — watch out for those who cause divisions.

16.title: Doxology
16.context: Doxology — Paul ends with a beautiful word of praise. To God be glory forever.

1.title: Greeting
1.context: Greeting — even to a deeply messed-up church, Paul calls them 'sanctified in Christ Jesus'.

1.title: Divisions in the Church
1.context: Divisions in the church — 'I follow Paul, I follow Apollos'. Pride dressed in spiritual clothing.

1.title: The Wisdom of the Cross
1.context: The wisdom of the cross — 'The foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom'.

3.title: The Foundation Is Christ
3.context: The foundation is Christ — 'No one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid'.

5.title: Sexual Immorality in the Church
5.context: Sexual immorality — the church cannot tolerate open sin. 'Get rid of the old yeast'.

6.title: Lawsuits Among Believers
6.context: Lawsuits among believers — Christians shouldn't take each other to pagan courts.

7.title: Concerning Marriage
7.context: Concerning marriage — Paul's fullest teaching: marriage is good, singleness also good.

8.title: Food Sacrificed to Idols
8.context: Food sacrificed to idols — Christian freedom is limited by a brother's weak conscience.

9.title: Paul's Apostolic Rights
9.context: Paul's apostolic rights — he has them but gives them up, 'so as not to hinder the gospel'.

10.title: Warnings from Israel's History
10.context: Warnings from Israel — Paul uses wilderness failures as warnings. 'These things were written for our instruction'.

11.title: Order in Worship
11.context: Order in worship — Paul addresses men and women's roles in worship. Still much-debated today.

11.title: The Lord's Supper
11.context: Paul corrects abuses of the Lord's Supper at Corinth. The meal proclaims Christ's death until he comes — a constant rehearsal of the gospel.

12.title: Spiritual Gifts
12.context: Spiritual gifts — one Spirit, many gifts, given as the Spirit determines.

12.title: One Body, Many Members
12.context: One body, many members — diversity within unity. Every part needs every other part.

13.title: The Way of Love
13.context: The love chapter — read at countless weddings, but originally written to a divided church to remind them love is the only true mark of being Spirit-filled.

14.title: Prophecy and Tongues
14.context: Prophecy and tongues — Paul redirects gift use toward edification, not display.

15.title: The Resurrection of Christ
15.context: The resurrection chapter — the foundation of Christian faith. 'If Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile.' The most fundamental defense in Scripture.

15.title: The Resurrection Body
15.context: The resurrection body — perishable sown, imperishable raised.

16.title: The Collection and Final Words
16.context: The collection — practical mission woven into the final exhortations.

1.title: The God of All Comfort
1.context: The God of all comfort — Paul comforted in trouble so he can comfort others.

2.title: Forgiveness for the Offender
2.context: Forgiveness for the offender — the church must restore the repentant, not crush them.

2.title: The Aroma of Christ
2.context: The aroma of Christ — 'God always leads us in triumphal procession in Christ'.

3.title: Ministers of the New Covenant
3.context: Ministers of the new covenant — Moses' glory faded; ours endures.

4.title: Treasure in Jars of Clay
4.context: 'We have this treasure in jars of clay' — Paul's deepest portrait of ministry: fragile vessels carrying eternal glory.

5.title: Our Heavenly Dwelling
5.context: Our heavenly dwelling — Christians long for the eternal home with eyes of faith.

5.title: The Ministry of Reconciliation
5.context: The ministry of reconciliation — 'God was reconciling the world to himself in Christ'.

6.title: Unequally Yoked
6.context: Unequally yoked — applies to marriage, business partnerships, and deep alliances.

8.title: Generosity Encouraged
8.context: Macedonian generosity — 'Their extreme poverty welled up in rich generosity'.

9.title: Cheerful Givers
9.context: Cheerful givers — 'God loves a cheerful giver'.

10.title: Paul Defends His Ministry
10.context: Paul defends his ministry — gentle in person, sometimes sharp in writing.

11.title: Paul's Sufferings
11.context: Paul's sufferings — beaten, imprisoned, shipwrecked, in danger of death. Marks of authentic ministry.

12.title: Paul's Vision and Thorn
12.context: Paul's thorn in the flesh — three times he begs God to remove it. The answer: 'My grace is sufficient for you. My power is made perfect in weakness.'

13.title: Final Warnings
13.context: Final warnings — 'Examine yourselves'. A call for self-examination.

1.title: Greeting and the True Gospel
1.context: Greeting and the true gospel — Paul skips his usual thanks. Straight to the point: you're abandoning the gospel.

1.title: Paul's Apostolic Calling
1.context: Paul's apostolic calling — 'I received it not from any man, but from Jesus Christ'.

2.title: Paul Accepted by the Apostles
2.context: Paul accepted by the apostles — privately he and James, Peter, John agree on one gospel for all.

2.title: Paul Confronts Peter
2.context: Paul confronts Peter — Peter eats with Gentiles, then withdraws under pressure. Paul rebukes him publicly.

2.title: Justification by Faith
2.context: Justification by faith — Paul's classic statement: 'A person is justified not by works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ'.

3.title: By Faith, Like Abraham
3.context: Paul's exasperated cry: 'You foolish Galatians!' The argument that justification comes by faith and faith alone — an argument that fired the Reformation.

3.title: The Law and the Promise
3.context: Law and promise — Paul clarifies. The law doesn't cancel the promise; it serves as a guardian leading us to Christ.

4.title: Sons and Heirs
4.context: Sons and heirs — 'God sent his Son… to redeem those under the law'.

4.title: Hagar and Sarah
4.context: Hagar and Sarah — Paul's allegory: law produces slaves, promise produces free children.

5.title: Stand Firm in Freedom
5.context: Stand firm in freedom — 'Do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery'.

5.title: Spirit vs. Flesh
5.context: Spirit vs. flesh — the inner battlefield. 'Walk by the Spirit and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh'.

5.title: The Fruit of the Spirit
5.context: The fruit of the Spirit — nine traits that mark the Spirit-shaped life. Not nine separate fruits, but one fruit with nine flavors of Christlikeness.

6.title: Bearing One Another's Burdens
6.context: Bearing one another's burdens — 'In this way you will fulfill the law of Christ'.

1.title: Spiritual Blessings in Christ
1.context: Spiritual blessings in Christ — Ephesians' breathtaking opening. Chosen 'before the creation of the world'.

1.title: Paul's Prayer of Thanksgiving
1.context: Paul's prayer of thanksgiving — that they may 'know him better'. A prayer for every believer.

2.title: From Death to Life
2.context: 'You were dead in your transgressions and sins… but God made us alive with Christ.' Paul's most striking picture of salvation as resurrection.

2.title: Made One in Christ
2.context: Made one in Christ — 'Christ is our peace'. The wall of hostility broken down.

3.title: The Mystery of the Gospel
3.context: The mystery of the gospel — once hidden, now revealed: Gentiles share equally in Christ.

3.title: Prayer for Spiritual Strength
3.context: Prayer for spiritual strength — to grasp the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge.

4.title: Unity in the Body
4.context: Unity in the body — 'one body, one Spirit' — the foundation of Christian unity.

4.title: The Old and New Self
4.context: The old and new self — 'Put off falsehood, speak truth'. A practical list of repentance.

5.title: Walking in Love and Light
5.context: Walking in love and light — 'Live as children of light'.

5.title: Husbands and Wives
5.context: Husbands and wives — husband love as Christ loved the church; wife respect as the church submits to Christ.

6.title: Children and Parents
6.context: Children and parents — 'Obey your parents in the Lord'. God's view of the family.

6.title: The Armor of God
6.context: The armor of God — the Christian's struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against spiritual forces. Paul's battle gear is mostly defensive.

1.title: Thanksgiving and Prayer
1.context: Thanksgiving — Paul writes from prison full of joy. This is the 'joy letter'.

1.title: Christ Proclaimed in Chains
1.context: Christ proclaimed in chains — 'What has happened to me has actually served to advance the gospel'.

1.title: Worthy of the Gospel
1.context: Worthy of the gospel — Christian life should match the gospel that saved us.

2.title: Christ's Humility
2.context: The Christ-hymn — the New Testament's most condensed declaration of who Jesus is and what he did. Likely an early church hymn Paul incorporated.

2.title: Shining as Lights
2.context: Shining as lights — be 'children of God without fault in a warped generation'.

2.title: Timothy and Epaphroditus
2.context: Timothy and Epaphroditus — Paul's most cherished co-workers. The treasure of spiritual friendship.

3.title: Knowing Christ
3.context: Knowing Christ — 'I consider everything a loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ'.

3.title: Pressing On
3.context: Pressing on — 'I press toward the goal for the prize of the upward call'.

4.title: Stand Firm in the Lord
4.context: Stand firm in the Lord — 'Beloved, this is how you should stand firm'.

4.title: Anxious for Nothing
4.context: 'Do not be anxious about anything, but pray about everything.' A prison letter's prescription for peace — written by a man in chains.

4.title: Thanks for the Philippians' Gift
4.context: Thanks for the gift — 'I have learned to be content whatever the circumstances'.

1.title: Greeting and Thanksgiving
1.context: Greeting and thanksgiving — Paul greets and praises this church for their faith and love.

1.title: The Supremacy of Christ
1.context: The Colossian Christ-hymn — declaring Christ as creator, sustainer, head of the church, and reconciler of all things. Christology in poetic compression.

1.title: Paul's Labor for the Church
1.context: Paul's labor for the church — even in prison, he serves the church gladly.

2.title: Beware of False Teaching
2.context: Beware of false teaching — 'Let no one deceive you with smooth talk'.

2.title: Freedom from Human Rules
2.context: Freedom from human rules — Christians no longer bound by food laws and special days.

3.title: Living as New People
3.context: Living as new people — 'Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things'.

3.title: Christian Households
3.context: Christian households — relationships in Christ between spouses, children, and workers.

4.title: Prayer and Witness
4.context: Prayer and witness — 'Pray for us, that God may open a door for our message'.

4.title: Final Greetings
4.context: Final greetings — Paul lists his co-workers. Even in prison, he is not alone.

1.title: Thanksgiving for the Thessalonians
1.context: Thanksgiving — one of Paul's earliest letters, praising a young church.

2.title: Paul's Ministry
2.context: Paul's ministry — 'We were gentle among you, like a nursing mother caring for her children'.

3.title: Timothy's Encouraging Report
3.context: Timothy's encouraging report — they're standing firm. Paul rejoices.

4.title: A Life Pleasing to God
4.context: A life pleasing to God — including specific words on sexual holiness.

4.title: The Coming of the Lord
4.context: The coming of the Lord — one of Paul's fullest descriptions of Christ's return. 'The Lord himself will descend from heaven'.

5.title: Be Children of Light
5.context: Be children of light — 'Let us not sleep, but be awake and sober'.

5.title: Final Instructions
5.context: Final instructions — 'Rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks in all circumstances'.

1.title: Comfort in Persecution
1.context: Comfort in persecution — their endurance and faith make Paul boast.

2.title: The Man of Lawlessness
2.context: The Man of Lawlessness — Paul corrects false teaching: the rebellion must come first; the antichrist must be revealed.

2.title: Stand Firm
2.context: Stand firm — 'Hold to the teachings we passed on to you'.

3.title: Pray for Us
3.context: 'Pray for us' — even Paul needs intercession.

3.title: Warning Against Idleness
3.context: Warning against idleness — 'If anyone is not willing to work, let him not eat'.

1.title: Warning Against False Teachers
1.context: Warning against false teachers — Paul's first concern in writing to Ephesus.

1.title: Paul's Testimony
1.context: Paul's testimony — 'Of whom I am the chief'. The greatest gospel testimony.

2.title: Prayer for All People
2.context: Prayer for all people — 'Pray for kings and all those in authority'.

2.title: Men and Women in Worship
2.context: Men and women in worship — Paul's guidance for congregational order.

3.title: Qualifications for Overseers
3.context: Qualifications for overseers — 15 standards. Character before competence.

3.title: Qualifications for Deacons
3.context: Qualifications for deacons — those who serve must also meet spiritual standards.

4.title: Watch Out for False Teaching
4.context: Watch out for false teaching — 'In later times some will abandon the faith'.

5.title: Care for Widows and Elders
5.context: Care for widows and elders — treat older men like fathers, younger as brothers; older women like mothers, younger as sisters.

6.title: Slaves and the Love of Money
6.context: Slaves and the love of money — 'The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil'.

6.title: The Good Fight of Faith
6.context: The good fight of faith — 'Fight the good fight'. The Christian calling.

1.title: Guard the Good Deposit
1.context: Guard the good deposit — recalling Lois (grandmother) and Eunice (mother). Generational faith.

2.title: A Good Soldier of Christ
2.context: A good soldier of Christ — 'Endure hardship like a good soldier'.

2.title: An Approved Worker
2.context: An approved worker — 'Correctly handling the word of truth'. The goal of every Christian worker.

3.title: Godlessness in the Last Days
3.context: Godlessness in the last days — Paul lists end-time character traits. A mirror.

3.title: The Power of Scripture
3.context: The power of Scripture — 'All Scripture is God-breathed and useful'.

4.title: Preach the Word
4.context: Preach the word — 'In season and out of season'.

4.title: Paul's Final Words
4.context: Paul's final words — 'I have fought the good fight'. A martyr's deathbed summary of life lived for Christ.

1.title: Greeting and Elders Required
1.context: Greeting and elders required — Paul asks Titus to organize the Cretan churches.

2.title: What Sound Doctrine Looks Like
2.context: Sound doctrine — concrete guidance for old, young, slaves.

2.title: Grace That Trains Us
2.context: Grace that trains us — 'to renounce ungodliness'. Grace doesn't just forgive; it transforms behavior.

3.title: Good Works in the World
3.context: Good works in the world — Christian witness. 'Show true humility toward all'.

1.title: Greeting to Philemon
1.context: Greeting to Philemon — a private letter from prison to a wealthy believer.

1.title: Paul's Plea for Onesimus
1.context: Paul's plea for Onesimus — a runaway slave now a believer. Paul asks for his reception in a new identity.

1.title: Receive Him as You Would Me
1.context: Receive him as you would me — radical request that quietly subverts slavery itself.

1.title: God Has Spoken by His Son
1.context: The opening of Hebrews: long ago God spoke by the prophets in many ways; in these last days he has spoken by a Son — the radiance of his glory.

1.title: The Son Superior to Angels
1.context: A chain of seven OT quotations argues the Son's name is far above the angels — they are ministering spirits; he sits at the right hand of Majesty.

2.title: Pay Closer Attention
2.context: The first warning of the letter: if a message spoken through angels was binding, how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation?

2.title: Made Perfect Through Suffering
2.context: Jesus was made for a little while lower than the angels so he might taste death for everyone — bringing many sons to glory.

2.title: A Brother and Faithful High Priest
2.context: He does not help angels but Abraham's offspring — made like his brothers in every respect, a merciful and faithful high priest.

3.title: Greater Than Moses
3.context: Moses was faithful in God's house as a servant; Christ is faithful as a Son over God's house — and we are his house.

3.title: Do Not Harden Your Hearts
3.context: Quoting Psalm 95 — today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion in the wilderness.

4.title: A Promised Rest Still Stands
4.context: The promise of entering his rest still stands; the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword.

4.title: A High Priest Who Sympathises
4.context: We have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens — let us draw near to the throne of grace with confidence.

7.title: Melchizedek the Priest-King
7.context: Melchizedek met Abraham, blessed him, received a tenth — king of Salem, king of righteousness, king of peace, without genealogy.

7.title: A Better Priesthood
7.context: If perfection had come through the Levitical priesthood, why would another priest arise in the order of Melchizedek? — appointed by the power of an indestructible life.

7.title: A Priest Forever
7.context: Sworn in by an oath, holding his priesthood permanently — he is able to save to the uttermost, always living to intercede.

8.title: Minister in the True Tent
8.context: We have such a high priest, seated at the right hand of the Majesty in heaven — minister in the true tabernacle.

8.title: A New Covenant
8.context: Quoting Jeremiah 31 — the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant; I will put my laws on their hearts.

9.title: The Earthly Sanctuary
9.context: The first covenant had regulations for worship and an earthly tent — the Holy Place, then the Most Holy, entered once a year.

9.title: Christ Entered with His Own Blood
9.context: Christ entered once for all into the holy places, securing eternal redemption — purifying our conscience to serve the living God.

9.title: Once for All to Bear Many Sins
9.context: Just as it is appointed for man to die once and after that comes judgement — so Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many.

10.title: A Shadow of Good Things to Come
10.context: If the law could perfect through repeated sacrifices, would they not have ceased? Christ's single offering perfects forever those being sanctified.

10.title: Sat Down at God's Right Hand
10.context: Every priest stands daily offering sacrifices that can never take away sins — but he, after offering one sacrifice for sins, sat down at the right hand of God.

10.title: Draw Near with Confidence
10.context: Brothers, since we have confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus — let us hold fast our confession and stir one another to love.

10.title: Warning Against Deliberate Sin
10.context: If we go on sinning deliberately after receiving the truth, no sacrifice for sins is left — only a fearful expectation of judgement.

10.title: Recall Your Earlier Sufferings
10.context: Recall the former days when, after being enlightened, you endured a hard struggle with sufferings — the righteous shall live by faith.

11.title: Faith Is Assurance of Things Hoped For
11.context: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen — by it the people of old received their commendation.

11.title: Abel, Enoch, Noah
11.context: The earliest witnesses to faith — without faith it is impossible to please God; whoever draws near must believe that he exists and rewards.

11.title: Abraham and Sarah
11.context: Abraham obeyed by faith and went out, not knowing where; Sarah by faith received power to conceive — they desired a better country, a heavenly one.

11.title: Moses and the Exodus
11.context: Moses by faith refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; Israel by faith crossed the Red Sea as on dry land — the Egyptians, attempting to do the same, were drowned.

11.title: A Cloud of Witnesses
11.context: Time would fail to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, David and the prophets — through faith they conquered kingdoms; others were sawn in two, wandered destitute.

12.title: Looking to Jesus, the Founder of Faith
12.context: Surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight — looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith.

12.title: Discipline of a Loving Father
12.context: Lift your drooping hands and strengthen your weak knees — the Lord disciplines the one he loves and chastises every son he receives.

12.title: See That No One Falls Short
12.context: See to it that no one fails to obtain the grace of God — that no root of bitterness springs up, that no one is sexually immoral or unholy like Esau.

12.title: You Have Come to Mount Zion
12.context: You have not come to a mountain that may be touched — but to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, and to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant.

12.title: Do Not Refuse Him Who Is Speaking
12.context: His voice once shook the earth; now he has promised to shake the heavens also — therefore, since we receive a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us offer acceptable worship.

13.title: Brotherly Love and Hospitality
13.context: Let brotherly love continue; do not neglect to show hospitality — by this some have entertained angels unawares.

13.title: Remember Your Leaders
13.context: Remember those who led you and spoke the word of God — Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.

13.title: Outside the Camp
13.context: Jesus suffered outside the gate to sanctify the people through his own blood — therefore let us go to him outside the camp, bearing his reproach.

13.title: Obey Your Leaders
13.context: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls as those who will give an account.

13.title: The God of Peace
13.context: May the God of peace, who brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great Shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant — equip you with everything good.

5.title: Christ Appointed High Priest
5.context: Every high priest is chosen from among men; Christ did not exalt himself — God appointed him a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.

5.title: Dull of Hearing
5.context: About this we have much to say but it is hard to explain — by now you ought to be teachers, yet you need someone to teach you the basics again.

6.title: Press On to Maturity
6.context: Therefore let us leave the elementary doctrine of Christ and go on to maturity — not laying again a foundation.

6.title: Falling Away Cannot Be Restored
6.context: It is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened and then have fallen away, to restore them again to repentance — the letter's sharpest warning.

6.title: We Are Confident of Better Things
6.context: Despite the warning, we feel sure of better things in your case, things that belong to salvation — God is not unjust to overlook your work.

6.title: God's Promise as an Anchor
6.context: God swore by himself, by an oath that cannot change — this hope is a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, entering inside the curtain.

1.title: Trials and Wisdom
1.context: James opens with a paradox: count trials all joy. Why? Because they produce the very steadfastness that completes faith.

1.title: Hearing and Doing the Word
1.context: Hearing and doing — 'Do not merely listen, deceiving yourselves'. James's core conviction.

2.title: Do Not Show Favoritism
2.context: Do not show favoritism — 'Don't show favoritism'. One of James's most practical warnings.

2.title: Faith Without Works Is Dead
2.context: 'Faith without works is dead' — James's central thesis. Not contradicting Paul's 'justified by faith' but completing it: real faith always works.

3.title: Taming the Tongue
3.context: The tongue — James's vivid warning about the destructive power of speech: fire, poison, an untamable beast hanging in our jaws.

3.title: Wisdom from Above
3.context: Wisdom from above — 'pure, peaceable, gentle'. Earthly wisdom is bitter and divisive.

4.title: Submit to God
4.context: Submit to God — 'Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you'.

4.title: Do Not Boast About Tomorrow
4.context: Do not boast about tomorrow — 'You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes'.

5.title: Warning to the Rich
5.context: Warning to the rich — James's sharpest words, in the prophetic tradition.

5.title: The Prayer of Faith
5.context: The prayer of faith — 'The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective'. Elijah as example.

1.title: Born to a Living Hope
1.context: Peter writes to 'exiles scattered abroad' — every Christian's true identity. Our home is not here; we live as resident aliens until Christ returns.

1.title: Be Holy
1.context: Be holy — and love one another. The two marks of the Christian.

2.title: A Chosen People
2.context: 'You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood' — Exodus 19's words for Israel are now spoken over the church. We inherit Sinai through Christ.

2.title: Living as Aliens
2.context: Living as aliens — 'Dear friends, I urge you, as aliens and strangers'.

2.title: Servants and Masters
2.context: Servants and masters — Christ as the example in unjust suffering.

3.title: Husbands and Wives
3.context: Husbands and wives — mutual respect in Christian marriage.

3.title: Suffering for Righteousness
3.context: Suffering for righteousness — 'Even if you should suffer for what is right, you are blessed'.

4.title: Suffering for Christ
4.context: Suffering for Christ — suffering is part of Christian life, not a deviation from it.

4.title: Sharing in Christ's Sufferings
4.context: 'Do not be surprised at the fiery trial.' Suffering is part of Christian life, not an interruption to it. Peter — soon to die for Christ — knows this firsthand.

5.title: Charge to the Elders
5.context: Charge to the elders — Peter writes as a fellow elder. Peer to peer.

5.title: Final Exhortations
5.context: Final exhortations — 'Cast all your anxiety on him'. Peter's shepherd's heart.

1.title: Growing in Grace
1.context: Growing in grace — the ladder of spiritual growth: faith, virtue, knowledge, self-control…

1.title: Eyewitnesses of His Majesty
1.context: Eyewitnesses of his majesty — Peter saw the Transfiguration.

2.title: False Teachers
2.context: False teachers — using the same tradition Jude does. Their judgment is sure.

3.title: The Day of the Lord
3.context: Why does the Lord delay? 'He is patient with you, not wishing that any should perish.' What looks like silence is actually mercy.

1.title: The Word of Life
1.context: The Word of life — 'We have heard, we have seen with our eyes, our hands have touched'. The strongest eyewitness claim.

1.title: Walking in the Light
1.context: Walking in the light — 'If we claim fellowship with him yet walk in darkness, we lie'.

2.title: Christ Our Advocate
2.context: Christ our Advocate — 'If anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father'.

2.title: Do Not Love the World
2.context: Do not love the world — 'Do not love the world or anything in the world'.

2.title: Warning Against Antichrists
2.context: Warning against antichrists — responding to early Gnostic-style teaching.

3.title: Children of God
3.context: Children of God — 'See what kind of love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God'.

3.title: Love One Another
3.context: Love one another — 'This is the message you heard from the beginning'.

4.title: Test the Spirits
4.context: Test the spirits — don't believe every spiritual claim; test it by the truth about Christ.

4.title: God Is Love
4.context: 'God is love' — one of two of Scripture's deepest declarations of God's essence (the other: 'God is spirit', John 4:24).

5.title: Faith That Conquers
5.context: Faith that conquers — 'This is the victory that has overcome the world, even our faith'.

5.title: That You May Know
5.context: That you may know — 'I write these things… that you may know you have eternal life'.

1.title: Walking in Truth and Love
1.context: Walking in truth and love — love walks according to truth; truth is love's root.

1.title: Warning Against False Teachers
1.context: Warning against deceivers — 'Whoever does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God'.

1.title: Commendation of Gaius
1.context: Commendation of Gaius — a brother who hosted traveling missionaries.

1.title: Diotrephes's Evil
1.context: Diotrephes's evil — refusing hospitality to gospel workers. Church politics turning ugly.

1.title: Good Testimony of Demetrius
1.context: Good testimony of Demetrius — a missionary praised by the whole church. Spiritual reputation.

1.title: Contend for the Faith
1.context: Contend for the faith — 'I had to write urging you to contend for the faith'.

1.title: Examples of Judgment
1.context: Examples of judgment — Jude cites Israel, fallen angels, Sodom.

1.title: Warning About the Last Days
1.context: Warning about the last days — 'In the last days there will be scoffers'.

1.title: Doxology
1.context: Doxology — 'To him who is able to keep you from stumbling' — one of the most majestic in the New Testament.

1.title: Revelation of Jesus Christ
1.context: Revelation opens — exiled John on Patmos receives visions that pull back the curtain on cosmic history. The Bible's most symbolic book begins.

1.title: John's Vision of Christ
1.context: John's vision of Christ — the Lord appears in glory; John falls at his feet as dead.

2.title: To Ephesus
2.context: To Ephesus — 'You have forsaken the love you had at first'. Doctrinal correctness without love.

2.title: To Smyrna
2.context: To Smyrna — no rebuke. The persecuted church receives only Jesus' commendation.

2.title: To Pergamum
2.context: To Pergamum — 'Where Satan has his throne'. A city full of idols.

2.title: To Thyatira
2.context: To Thyatira — tolerating 'Jezebel'. False teaching unchecked.

3.title: To Sardis
3.context: To Sardis — 'You have a reputation of being alive, but you are dead'. The harshest verdict.

3.title: To Philadelphia
3.context: To Philadelphia — no rebuke. 'I will not blot out your name'.

3.title: To Laodicea
3.context: To Laodicea — lukewarm. The state Jesus cannot stomach.

4.title: The Throne in Heaven
4.context: The throne vision — beneath all the chaos of history, God still reigns. Heaven's first response is worship: 'Holy, holy, holy.'

5.title: The Lamb Worthy
5.context: The Lamb opens the seals — only 'the Lamb who was slain' is worthy. The key to all history is the cross.

6.title: The Six Seals
6.context: The six seals — the four horsemen of the Apocalypse. The end times begin.

7.title: The 144,000 Sealed
7.context: The 144,000 sealed — 12,000 from each tribe. God preserves his people.

8.title: The First Four Trumpets
8.context: The first four trumpets — disasters intensify. Judgment escalates.

9.title: Trumpets Five and Six
9.context: Trumpets five and six — locusts and horsemen. Judgment reaches its peak.

10.title: The Angel and the Little Scroll
10.context: The angel and the little scroll — John eats it. 'Sweet as honey in my mouth, but bitter in my stomach'.

11.title: The Two Witnesses
11.context: The two witnesses — testifying for three and a half years before being killed and resurrected.

12.title: The Woman and the Dragon
12.context: The woman and the dragon — Israel, Christ, Satan. The cosmic battle behind biblical history.

13.title: The Beast from the Sea
13.context: The beast from the sea — the Antichrist. One of the most famous apocalyptic images.

14.title: The Lamb on Mount Zion
14.context: The Lamb on Mount Zion — the 144,000 sing a new song before the Lamb.

15.title: The Seven Last Plagues
15.context: The seven last plagues — echoing the Exodus. God's final judgment.

17.title: Babylon the Great
17.context: Babylon the Great — the symbol of the world system that rejects God.

19.title: Hallelujah in Heaven
19.context: Hallelujah in heaven — the only time the word appears in the New Testament. Four times in this chapter.

19.title: The Rider on the White Horse
19.context: The rider on the white horse — Christ's triumphant return. The New Testament begins with a manger and ends with a throne.

20.title: The Thousand Years
20.context: The thousand years — Satan bound, the saints reigning with Christ. Much-debated, deeply hopeful.

20.title: The Great White Throne
20.context: The Great White Throne — all the dead judged according to what they had done.

21.title: A New Heaven and Earth
21.context: 'A new heaven and a new earth' — the Bible's deepest hope fulfilled. God dwells with his people; tears, death, and pain are undone forever.

21.title: The New Jerusalem
21.context: The New Jerusalem — a city descending from God. Pearl gates, golden streets.

22.title: The River of Life
22.context: The river of life — 'For the healing of the nations'. Scripture comes full circle to Eden.

22.title: I Am Coming Soon
22.context: Scripture's final promise: 'Behold, I am coming soon!' The church's two-millennium response: 'Come, Lord Jesus.'
